data.title: My favourite German word
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了在人工智能工具逐渐取代人类阅读和信息获取的背景下，精心撰写和编排文档的意义。作者同事质疑，如果人们不再阅读这些文档，精心制作是否还有必要。文章指出，年轻一代缺乏自主查找和应用信息的能力，而人们普遍期待即时、定制化的答案，甚至愿意牺牲质量和可靠性。作者进一步讨论了"Gegenstand"（德语，意为“物体”或“对象”）一词，强调物体具有独立于人类意志的特性，通过与物体的互动，人们能认识自我和世界。好的设计应在适应人类需求与保留物体自身特性之间取得平衡，过度迎合的设计则可能导致不便和不适。最终，文章反思了高质量文档和良好设计的必要性，强调物体和现实的独立性与完整性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对文章内容及语言学问题的多角度讨论

不同观点：
• **对文章的赞赏与质疑**：
   - [leecommamichael] 赞赏文章，并通过个人经验说明低技术工具（如纸笔）有助于保持创造性，而高科技工具则可能抑制创造性。
   - [bryanlarsen] 指出文章前后内容存在矛盾：文章前半部分说旧的文档方式不再适用，后半部分又说好的文档方式仍然有效。

• **对语言和翻译的讨论**：
   - [llopium] 指出 "Gegenstand" 只是 "object" 的意思，并解释其在英语中的使用历史。
   - [jhoechtl] 提到德语中有多种以 "-stand" 结尾的词。
   - [gerdesj] 分享自己学习德语词 "Gewerbegebiet" 和 "Ausfahrt" 的经历。
   - [pflenker] 幽默地指出德语中许多词只是 "stuff"（东西）的组合，如 "Flugzeug"（飞机）。
   - [niemandhier] 认为 "Gegenstand" 更准确的翻译是 "a stand around"，并解释 "Widerstand" 的含义。
   - [masswerk] 指出英语中对象（objects）因其抵抗性（resistance）引起人们注意，类似于德语中的 "Widerstand"。
   - [yoz-y] 提问是否可以说一个对象 "站在对面" 就是 "反对"（objecting）你。

• **对LLM（大型语言模型）和文档的讨论**：
   - [andyferris] 认为当前 "为LLM写文档" 的趋势实际上反映了缺乏简洁可导航的文档，并对此趋势持乐观态度。
   - [exiguus] 担心LLM未来使用的训练数据质量下降，因为未来数据可能由LLM生成。

补充讨论：
• 语言学和文化背景的讨论是评论中的一个亮点，尤其是德语词汇的解析和个人学习经历的分享。
• 对文章内容的不同解读和质疑反映了对技术变革和工具使用影响的深层次思考。
• 对LLM和文档编写的讨论揭示了对新技术发展及其潜在问题的关注。

44613268.article_content:
My favourite German word
Â¶
30th June 2025
A documentation colleague recently challenged me with a question:
Nowadays, more and more people reach for an LLM tool to provide the information they want. If human beings donât actually read it, what is the point of writing and structuring documentation for humans?
Newer generations (she said) are becoming unskilled at finding information for themselves. They seem less able to digest what they find, to apply it to their problems. But itâs not just that:
everybody
seems to expect answers that are closely tailored to
their
particular situation, level of understanding and so on, and to get the answers
now
. And, many of them are willing to give up guarantees of quality and reliability in exchange of ease-of-use and customised responses.
So why should we take painstaking care in the creation of high-quality documentation?
A lot of recent discussion in documentation circles and forums has swirled uneasily around these topics. A popular and gloomy version of my colleagueâs line of thought is: âWhat is the point of my job?â
Good question.
Gegenstand
Â¶
My favourite word in the German language is
Gegenstand
, for
object
or
thing
.
I like it because it makes objectivity an
active principle
.
Gegenstand
, âstand-againstâ. An object is something that
stands against
you. Itâs not you. Itâs outside you. It has its own rules. It doesnât conform to your desires. You run up against it, and it resists.
Objects arenât just inert
stuff
â they do something. Even better,
Gegenstand
shows how objects help define
us
. I know what I am, what the limits of myself are, because I am able to come up against resistant objects. Thatâs how I know and have a sense of my own body, its extension in space, where it ends and where the world begins.
I am able to have a self in the first place only because the world of objects is there to stand against me.
The nature of things
Â¶
Gegenstand
gives objects and reality a kind of integrity. I have to respect them. They do not yield to my will just because I want them to. They have a nature that belongs to them. If I want to do something with them, Iâm going to have to work
on their terms
to do it.
A lever is a lever because it resists.
Realityâs resistance is what makes it possible to work with things at all. Every tool and machine that ever existed worked by being a stubbornly resistant
Gegenstand
.
Shared reality
Â¶
A
Gegenstand
is an object
for me
- an object of my experience.
But objects are objects for everyone. They are there to stand against
everybody
. Itâs not just that we have a shared experience of objects â our experience and knowledge
of each other
is also only possible because we inhabit a world of shared objects to stand against.
Design, fit and resistance
Â¶
Good design is magnificent because it takes resistant materials, unyielding constraints, and successfully gives them a form that works for us.
Itâs a pleasure to pick up something â a knife, a camera, anything â that simultaneously
fits and resists
the hand, in just the right ways. Good clothes fit and resist the body.
The pleasure is not just in the fitting, but in the fitting
and
resistance.
Bad design
Â¶
Something that
resists unpleasantly
, like an uncomfortable chair, is bad design. It only resists, and fails to fit. (We have enough of those things in our lives.)
But, bad design is also when things are made
to fit too much
.
In the 1980s, a strange thing started to happen to physical products, and continues today. The idea that objects should fit to human needs began to be interpreted as meaning that they should
literally fit the shape of the hand
. Parts of everyday products â on bicycles, umbrellas, cameras â were increasingly given hand-shaped
grips
.
A camera today will often have a grip closely contoured to the fingers of the hand. In one way this does make the camera easier to hold â but literally
only in one way
. Only with the right hand, and only in one particular way, so tough luck if that doesnât suit you â for example if you have a physical disability. Holding it any other way (and there are many good ways of holding a camera) is made more difficult, unsafe and uncomfortable. (Similarly, the asymmetric computer mice that became popular a couple of decades ago were as unpleasant in the left hand as a shoe on the wrong foot.)
These objects are
over-fitted
.
Servile objects
Â¶
Our hands, that evolved over millions of years, can hold almost any suitably-sized object safely and comfortably. Things donât need to be specially fitted to the hand; our hands are happy to meet and hold anything that doesnât actively resist them.
In fact, they donât want objects to be over-fitted.
Over-fitted objects are servile
. They have a creepy character. They are craven and eager to please, and give up their own confidence of form, that would allow us, with our splendidly adaptive hands, to hold them in multiple different ways. Their d

data.title: Tokyo's retro shotengai arcades are falling victim to gentrification
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述东京老旧的商业街区（shotengai）正面临被城市开发、人口减少和便利消费文化取代的困境。以Tsutomu Nishiwaki的 noodle shop为例，这家有着60年历史的家族面店即将因社区重建而关闭。随着开发商建造新公寓和商业设施，许多传承几代的小商店、餐馆和酒吧将消失。尽管一些商家试图通过怀旧吸引游客，但大多数像Tateishi Nakamise这样的街区正逐渐被现代化取代。文章反映了当地居民对未来发展的复杂情感，有些人期待通过出售物业获得养老资金，而另一些人则惋惜传统社区文化的消失。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：日本传统商业街区（如 shotengai 拱廊街）的衰落及其原因和影响

不同观点：
• **衰落原因：需求不足**  
  *decimalenough* 认为，shotengai 自1990年代以来已经衰落或濒临消亡，主要原因是需求不足，而不是绅士化。消费者更倾向于去一站式购物场所，如超市和便利店，而不是访问无法在价格上竞争的专卖零售商。

• **便利性发展的影响**  
  *litia_shi* 指出，以便利为导向的开发常常将社区从传统商业中心拉走，导致传统商业街区的衰落。

• **城市再生与住房可负担性**  
  *lmm* 认为东京通过不断重建和再生保持了其宜居性和住房的可负担性，并希望这种趋势继续下去。

• **前瞻性发展与历史保护的平衡**  
  *epolanski* 强调，日本既重视传统和历史，又积极推进城市发展和项目开发，这种前瞻性的态度虽然可能导致一些旧街区的消失，但有助于减少通勤需求，从长远来看是必要的。

• **旧商业街的现状**  
  *kazinator* 指出，日本各地仍然有很多破旧的老商业街，即使在离东京不远的地方也是如此，暗示衰落现象并非普遍。

• **新建设项目的影响与小企业援助**  
  *pilingual* 对新建设项目（如大阪火车站）持批评态度，认为这些项目浪费空间和资源，建议日本参考国外案例，如圣塔罗（Sanatana Row），为小企业提供过渡帮助。

• **特定区域的变化**  
  *firefax* 提到，东京秋叶原一带的小型零件商店也在缩减或消失，反映了类似趋势。

• **现实需求与浪漫期望的冲突**  
  *pinoy420* 认为，人们常常浪漫化地期望老旧商业街区继续存在，但忽略了这些街区是由真实的人运营的，他们有现代需求和变化的价值观，因此其 longevity（寿命）不可避免地会减少。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于如何平衡城市发展与历史保护，特别是在小企业和传统街区的保护与现代化建设之间找到合适的平衡点。
- 一些评论者关注新建项目的实际效果与资源利用效率，建议参考国外成功的案例以提供更好的解决方案。
- 另一个讨论点是东京等大城市的宜居性与住房可负担性，部分评论者对此持积极态度，认为持续的城市再生有助于保持城市活力。

Tsutomu Nishiwaki at his noodle shop in Tateishi Nakamise, an ageing shopping arcade in eastern Tokyo, Japan.
Photograph: Justin McCurry/The Guardian
View image in fullscreen
Tsutomu Nishiwaki at his noodle shop in Tateishi Nakamise, an ageing shopping arcade in eastern Tokyo, Japan.
Photograph: Justin McCurry/The Guardian
Japan
‘Cult of convenience’: how Tokyo’s retro shotengai arcades are falling victim to gentrification
Across Japan covered shopping arcades are in a losing battle against property developers, depopulation and consumer culture
Justin McCurry
in Tokyo
Thu 17 Jul 2025 21.32 EDT
Last modified on Fri 18 Jul 2025 21.30 EDT
Share
T
sutomu Nishiwaki raises the shutters of his store, the rattle marking the start of a new day at a shopping arcade in Tokyo. He wheels a display case into the foreground and stands behind the counter, framed by a sign proclaiming that this is a family-run noodle store.
It is a ritual Nishiwaki has been performing almost daily for 60 years. But like the fresh noodles its owner makes every morning, the store has a limited shelf life: in a few years from now, the 80-year-old will pull down the shutters for the last time.
Dozens of shops, restaurants and bars lining the streets of Tateishi Nakamise, a covered shopping arcade – or
shotengai
– in the capital’s eastern suburbs will make way for a new development. It will transform the skyline, but also change beyond recognition an entire community whose roots lie in the destruction caused by the second world war.
Across Tokyo and other Japanese cities, shotengai that sprung up during the Showa era [1926-1989] are in a losing battle against property developers, depopulation and a consumer culture that demands convenience.
On one side of the local railway station, a tall screen partially hides cranes preparing the ground for apartment blocks, shops and a multi-storey local government office. On the other, families that have run shops, bars and restaurants for two or three generations are bracing for the inevitable arrival of the wrecking balls.
View image in fullscreen
Ads for noodles at Tsutomu Nishiwaki’s shop in Tateishi Nakamise shopping arcade, Tokyo.
Photograph: Justin McCurry/The Guardian
“It is a shame that the shotengai will disappear,” says Nishiwaki, who is also head of a local association of business owners. “Half of me is hopeful about the future, but the other half regrets what is happening to the neighbourhood. I think people around here just want to get it over and done with.”
They include Koichi Ozaki, whose family run an
izakaya
pub they accept will probably not survive the redevelopment. The threats of
powerful earthquakes
, fires and, in this part of eastern Tokyo, catastrophic flooding have convinced him that the destruction of the arcade’s dilapidated buildings is inevitable.
“In any case, people don’t shop in the same way any more,” Ozaki says. “We live in the age of the supermarket, and family-run stores are on their way out.”
The Tateishi redevelopment has divided locals, about two-thirds of whom see it as an opportunity to sell up and acquire a nest egg to see them through their twilight years. The rest say they will reopen elsewhere.
More parts of eastern Tokyo, known as shitamachi, literally “lower city”, are being disassembled and rebuilt in the image of the affluent Yamanote neighbourhoods on the city’s west side. Tateishi Nakamise was originally a black market set up after the US’s wartime bombing of eastern Tokyo that, on a single night in March 1945
killed
an estimated 100,000 people.
Before long, about 50 stores lined narrow streets packed with shoppers during the boom years of the 1960s and 1970s. “There were no supermarkets or convenience stores back then,” says Nishiwaki, who recalls a time when his father’s shop was one of about 20 noodle makers in the area.
View image in fullscreen
A store in Tateishi Nakamise shopping arcade in eastern Tokyo.
Photograph: Justin McCurry/The Guardian
“But there will be no third-generation owner,” he says of his shop, the last noodle seller still standing. “Supermarkets are cheaper and more convenient. Nakamise’s shops will disappear, and the local atmosphere along with it.”
Some shotengai have managed to market nostalgia, spurred by record numbers of foreign tourists keen to experience a less varnished side of Japanese urban life. Janjan Yokocho, a covered mall in Osaka, has capitalised on its Showa-era origins with retro game arcades, old-fashioned confectionery stores and parlour for
shogi
, a two-player game similar to chess.
Last year, businesses in Asakusa Kokusai Street declared their 3km shotengai, located near a Tokyo tourist hotspot, as the longest in
Japan
, claiming the title from the Tenjinbashisuji arcade in Osaka.
But success stories are rare: restaurant and shop owners in Tateishi Nakamise are not alone in wondering what the surge in new commercial developments will mean for their communities.

data.title: The .a file is a relic: Why static archives were a bad idea all along
data.author: eyalitki
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了C语言SDK中的静态链接库（.a文件）的缺点，以及为何静态档案并非理想解决方案。作者以自身在开发C语言SDK的经验为例，指出静态链接在满足客户需求方面的不足，尤其是在易用性、兼容性和维护性方面存在问题。动态链接库（.so文件）则提供了更好的灵活性，比如安全补丁可以通过更新库版本来实现。作者建议对ELF文件头进行更新，引入新的“静态捆绑对象”类型以替代现有的静态档案。文章最后强调，这是作者的个人观点，不代表其雇主的立场。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：静态链接与静态库（.a文件）的使用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• TuxSH认为，设计中依赖静态初始化顺序是不好的做法，并提到使用`-ffunction-sections -fdata-sections`和`-Wl,--gc-sections`可以解决一些未使用函数的问题，但这种做法在静态链接中使用较少。他还指出，依赖静态初始化本身就不是一个好主意。
• amiga386反驳称，TuxSH的例子过于牵强，并提出了一些针对日志模块的解决方案，如使用宏或特定的链接标志。他还强调了静态链接在防止动态链接器漏洞方面的优势。
• kazinator指出，.a文件可以加速大型软件的链接过程，因为它们处理依赖关系的方式与.o文件不同。他还提到Linux内核通过使用.a文件来减少链接时间和内存消耗。
• EE84M3i不理解为什么不能对.so文件进行静态链接，并询问在创建共享对象时丢失了哪些信息导致无法进行静态链接。
• tux3介绍了一种工具，可以将静态库中的所有对象文件合并成一个对象文件，以解决符号污染和大小问题，并认为这是一个临时解决方案。
• cryptonector认为静态链接停留在1978年的语义，而动态链接已经发展出许多新特性。他建议在.a文件中记录依赖元数据，以改进静态链接。
• dzaima建议创建一个工具，将多个.o文件合并成一个.o文件，通过将隐藏符号变为局部符号来解决符号泄露问题。
• stabbles提到，U-boot等项目已经解决了初始化函数的问题，并指出链接器会移除未使用的.o文件，这不是归档文件的问题。
• dale_glass分享了一个静态链接导致构造函数被多次调用和销毁的问题。
• flohofwoe认为，库文件本身不是问题，问题在于将预编译的二进制文件作为SDK发布。
• jhallenworld建议使用部分链接和剥离隐藏符号来解决私有符号问题。
• SanjayMehta指出，Unix起源于资源有限的PDP-11机器，当时静态链接是唯一可行的解决方案，称其为“一直是个坏主意”是不公平的。
• layer8质疑是否缺少.so文件的某些特性使其不适合作为静态链接的基础，并建议理想情况下应只发布一个库版本，让第三方选择静态或动态链接。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于静态链接和静态库的优缺点，特别是在符号冲突、初始化顺序和依赖处理方面。
• 一些评论者提供了技术解决方案，如使用特定链接标志、工具或设计模式来解决静态链接中的问题。
• 讨论还涉及静态链接和动态链接的历史背景和发展，以及如何在现代软件开发中更好地应用这些技术。

44613791.article_content:
The .a File is a Relic: Why Static Archives Were a Bad Idea All Along
Eyal Itkin
15 min read
·
2 days ago
--
Listen
Share
I’ll start with a confession: The C programming language is (still) my preferred language for networking/embedded projects. After 13+ years of development in C, this feeling decayed a bit, yet haven’t changed.
That said, in the last 4+ years I’ve been a core developer in a commercial C-based SDK, and oh boy, I did not expect the can of worms I had to handle in the SDK world. At some point I even “gave up” and started learning Rust, believing the C compilation ecosystem is a lost cause.
In this post I’ll try to cover the expectations our customers have from a C-based SDK, why static archives (
.a
files) will
never
be able to fulfil them, and my initial suggestion for a replacement static linking option.
Suggested update to the ELF file header — Addition of new “Static Bundle Object” type.
Just a brief disclaimer before we begin. While this article dives into lessons I learned, and bugs I witnessed, during my work as an SDK software engineer, this article expresses my
personal
thoughts and has nothing to do with my employer. I do believe that an industry shift into using a better static linking format will benefit also my employer (and surely make my life easier), yet this is still a personal opinion piece, and it does not reflect in any way the opinion or interest of my employer.
Now that we cleared this part, let’s begin.
What is a C-based SDK?
An SDK is a
S
oftware
D
evelopment
K
it. In layman’s terms, these are a set of libraries, header files, compilation definition helpers, and reference code snippets, focusing on a given software functionality. In our case, they provide a C-based programming API (Application Programming Interface) and ABI (Application Binary Interface) for customers to consume when they try to build a program that will leverage said functionality. As an example, this could be the famous, open-source, networking-oriented
DPDK
, or the closed-source, GPU-oriented
CUDA
.
An important observation here is that an SDK is more than just a set of libraries. We want our customers to be able to easily use these libraries, hence we are expected to provide as much aids as possible:
Include headers (
.h
files) — Without these files, no one can really compile against the provided libraries.
Pkg-config compilation definitions (
.pc
files) — An industry standard for providing compilation & linking related information.
Reference coding samples/applications — Simple C programs that showcase how to use the SDK’s API. These could be small samples that showcase a single user-scenario (sending a packet), or more robust applications that demonstrate a real-life use case (building a firewall).
Now that we covered the scope of the SDK, it is time to dive into the overlooked part of it, the libraries themselves.
Linking options — Dynamic vs Static
For most developers, this is the voodoo part that someone else in the team already set-up. All that was left for us is to include the needed header files and write our code accordingly, hoping that the program will compile successfully.
Somewhere long ago, usually at the early stages of the project, an architect or a tech lead decided how are we going to link against the SDKs we use. Will we dynamically link against them? Or will we use them statically instead?
There are different philosophies for each approach. On one side of the spectrum we can find Red Hat’s
stated dislike of this technology
:
Static linking is emphatically discouraged for all Red Hat Enterprise Linux releases. Static linking causes far more problems than it solves, and should be avoided at all costs.
And on the other, we can find Google’s policy, dictating that
everything
used in GCP’s production environments will be statically linked. This policy is evident for everyone who ever tried to compile and use
gRPC
on their own.
From the perspective of an SDK provider, we must not limit our customers. As such, we are expected to provide
both
the dynamic linking option, as well as the static linking one. And what will this mean?
Dynamic linking — Provide Shared Object (
.so
) libraries, as well as matching compilation (
.pc
) definitions.
Static linking — Provide Static Archive (
.a
) files, as well as matching compilation (
.pc
) definitions.
When we bundle the installation of our SDK for some Linux distros, we might decide to adapt it to the expected delivery per distro. For instance, when one installs
libpng
on Red Hat Linux, the installation will
not
include a static archive (
.a
) file, although it
will
include it on an Ubuntu installation.
Here’s a reminder of the gist of each of the loading methods.
Dynamic Linking 101
The library is taken pretty much “as-is”, and mapped to the virtual address space of the program at
load
time.
One notable advantage is that security fixes can be provided through updated library versions, as long as the ABI was kept intact (no breaking changes).

data.title: Show HN: The Magic of Code – book about the wonders and weirdness of computation
data.author: arbesman
data.article_summary: 《The Magic of Code》探讨了计算的奇妙与神秘，将计算视为一种人文博雅艺术，涉及语言、哲学、生物学以及我们的思维方式等方面。书中展示了计算如何广泛影响人类知识和生活的各个领域，强调其不仅仅是技术工具，更是一种理解世界的方式。读者可以通过提供的链接下载书籍样章，进一步了解其内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一本关于编程和代码魔法般魅力的书籍展开的评论和讨论。

不同观点：
• babblingfish认为这本书带来了清新的视角，强调编程旅程中的奇迹感，与其他乌托邦或反乌托邦的技术书籍形成对比。
• vegadw对书籍的引言部分表示赞赏，但担心引言过于吸引人，导致读者对书籍主体内容缺乏明确预期，特别是对于不熟悉编程的读者。
• upghost表达了共鸣，提到自己在职业中期对软件的幻灭感，而这本书成功唤醒了他对软件 magic 的重新认识，并表示会购买阅读。
• layer8指出当前社会对技术的担忧，但坚信未来几代人会重新发现代码的奇迹和价值，就像数学和物理一样。

补充讨论：
• 作者 arbesman 积极参与讨论，表示愿意回答任何关于书籍的问题，展现出开放和参与的态度。
• elwell 提到了 "Code: The Hidden Language of Computer Hardware and Software" 一书，认为其内容有趣，可能与讨论书籍有相似之处。
• lukyanovic 对书籍的前提表示兴趣，并提到编程与人文之间的鸿沟，期待看到书籍如何弥合这一差距。
• rramadass 将书籍与 Daniel Shiffman 的 "The Nature of Code" 进行比较，询问作者两者的异同。
• maxverse 提到曾在 Recurse Center 听过作者的演讲，并表示期待阅读书籍。
• ngruhn 仅对书籍封面表示赞赏，未深入讨论内容。
• handedness 提供了一个之前关于书籍网站的链接，未发表具体评论。

争议焦点：
• vegadw对书籍引言部分的效果存在疑虑，担心读者在未明确书籍主体内容的情况下失去阅读兴趣，而其他评论者如 babblingfish 和 upghost 则对书籍表示积极期待。
• 读者 rramadass 对书籍与类似主题书籍的比较，提出了对内容深度的潜在疑问。

整体来看，讨论主要围绕书籍的新颖性、对编程魅力的唤醒作用以及与类似书籍的比较展开，读者对书籍的期待和兴趣较为明显。

data.title: Yt-transcriber – Give a YouTube URL and get a transcription
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary:
**yt-transcriber** 是一个命令行工具，用户输入YouTube视频链接或本地音视频文件路径后，可获得转录文本，并支持发言者识别（开发中）、内容摘要和翻译。该工具利用开源AI技术，依赖Whisper模型进行本地转录，其他功能如摘要和翻译需结合OpenAI或Claude的API key。它支持多种音视频格式，并可通过Nix进行依赖管理。主要功能包括：

- 转录YouTube视频或本地文件
- 发言者识别（开发中）
- 文本摘要和翻译
- 支持多种模型大小以平衡处理时间和准确性

使用示例：
```bash
./yt-transcriber "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<youtube_id>" | summarize | translate Süddeutsch
```

依赖安装可通过Nix或手动配置，目前在Mac上测试通过。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• [paulirish] 提出可以使用 `yt-dlp` 直接获取YouTube自动生成的字幕，而无需重新转录，节省时间和资源。
• [MysticOracle] 认为对于英语语音转文字任务，NVIDIA的Parakeet-V2模型比Whisper更快、更准确，并提供了相关模型链接。
• [0points] 支持使用YouTube自带的AI转录功能，并指出由于有大量贡献者维护，`yt-dlp` 能持续适应YouTube的变更。

yt-transcriber
TUI app- Give it a YouTube URL (or a path to a video or audio file) and you get a transcription with possible speaker identification (WIP) and optional summary or translation, all thanks to open-source AI tooling and my lack of enough free time to watch content-sparse YouTube videos
features
transcribe YouTube videos by URL
output metadata about the video
speaker identification (probably using an LLM in conjunction with a speaker diarization library)
summarization via
summarize
(requires
OPENAI_API_KEY
to be set)
translation via
translate <language_name>
(requires
OPENAI_API_KEY
to be set)
can use almost any audio or video format that
ffmpeg
can handle as input, not just YouTube URLs
Test suite (run it with
yt-transcriber TEST
or
TEST=1 yt-transcriber
)
support for other video platforms
convert all this to a web service or web app
Speaker identification ("diarization"), summarization and translation will probably require an API key for Claude or OpenAI and/or one from Huggingface.
installation
NEW: If you have Nix installed or are running on NixOS, just symlink
yt-transcriber
,
summarize
and
translate
to any directory (usually
~/bin
or
XDG_BIN_HOME
which is usually
~/.local/bin
)
in your
PATH
and you're good to go (the last two require OPENAI_API_KEY to be
defined in your environment). The shell script will automatically procure all dependencies
deterministically and locally and cache them.
If you do not have Nix installed, I recommend using the Determinate Nix Installer from here:
https://github.com/DeterminateSystems/nix-installer
If you refuse to use Nix, you can try to install the following dependencies manually, but I make no guarantees:
python312
ffmpeg
glow
(
glow
is optional; if using the
--markdown|-md
argument with
summarize
, this makes things prettier in the terminal if you pipe to it)
The Python dependencies will be installed via pip into a venv cached in
$XDG_CACHE_HOME/yt-transcriber/.venv
and XDG_CACHE_HOME defaults to
~/.cache
if not set.
The Whisper model will be downloaded to
$XDG_CACHE_HOME/yt-transcriber/.whisper
.
the
flake.nix
file manages all deps, so just
nix develop
when in there.
./test_flake.sh
tests whether everything's set up correctly.
./yt_transcriber TEST
tests the app itself.
No app keys needed, Whisper runs locally.
Setup was only tested on Mac with a Nix install thus far. Will add tests for it working without Nix next.
example usage
./yt-transcriber
by itself will list options and usage (such as
-m modelsize
).
By default the app uses the
small
(second smallest) model; I recommend using at least
small
for better transcription results without costing too much extra processing time. The options are:
base
,
small
,
medium
,
large
,
large-v2
Transcript will be sent to stdout, so you can redirect it to a file or pipe it to another program such as the provided
./summarize[--markdown]
or
./translate [language]
scripts (see below).
If you set the
DEBUG
env var (to anything), you'll get additional logging/debug info to stderr.
#
(when in the project directory)
./yt-transcriber -m medium
"
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<youtube_id>
"
>
~
/Documents/transcript.txt
#
(when in the project directory)
./yt-transcriber -m small
"
/path/to/video/or/audio/file.mp4
"
|
./summarize
|
./translate Süddeutsch
>
~
/Documents/bavarian_german_summary.txt
#
(when yt-transcriber is on PATH)
yt-transcriber
"
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<youtube_id>
"
|
summarize --markdown
|
glow
For a full debug run try this:
#
(when in the project directory)
DEBUG=1 ./yt-transcriber -m small
"
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<youtube_id>
"
|
tee last_transcript.txt
|
./summarize

44646901.article_summary:
**yt-transcriber** 是一个命令行工具，用户输入YouTube视频链接或本地音视频文件路径后，可获得转录文本，并支持发言者识别（开发中）、内容摘要和翻译。该工具利用开源AI技术，依赖Whisper模型进行本地转录，其他功能如摘要和翻译需结合OpenAI或Claude的API key。它支持多种音视频格式，并可通过Nix进行依赖管理。主要功能包括：

- 转录YouTube视频或本地文件
- 发言者识别（开发中）
- 文本摘要和翻译
- 支持多种模型大小以平衡处理时间和准确性

使用示例：
```bash
./yt-transcriber "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<youtube_id>" | summarize | translate Süddeutsch
```

依赖安装可通过Nix或手动配置，目前在Mac上测试通过。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何检测"异常构建模式"及构建系统的设计与安全性，尤其是关于可重现构建和信任风险的讨论。

不同观点：
• [riffraff] 对系统如何检测"异常构建模式"表示好奇，尤其是如何识别如xz后门这样的问题。他提问系统是否依赖诸如"构建文件必须来自单个目录"或"不应使用存储库中已有的二进制文件"之类的规则，还是更通用的检测机制。

• [lrvick] 认为需要一个不可变的、确定性的、全源代码引导的操作系统来最小化信任风险，并介绍了ReprOS项目来解决此问题。该项目通过在一次性虚拟机中构建，并在主机上签署构件结果，以减少攻击风险。

• [simonw] 对项目表示兴奋，但指出需要一个web界面来减少使用Go CLI工具带来的摩擦。他还分享了通过"gsutil"命令获取构建列表的方法，并提供了相关Gist链接。

• [Flux159] 提到该系统是否要求通过CI系统而非开发者本地机器进行构建，并指出npm包的发布和Docker构建结果不一致的问题。他还询问该项目是否主要针对pypi、npm和crates，而忽略了Linux发行版如Debian的包。

• [WhatIsDukkha] 认为该项目是一个不彻底的措施，因为它不提供客户端构建功能。他提到Guix可以通过客户端机器重现上游二进制文件，并认为分布式重现能力更为优越。

• [Weethet] 质疑创建一个更狭窄版本的必要性，指出Nixpkgs已经有107158个打包的库和可执行文件，且Nix基础设施支持任意构建系统和创建Docker镜像。

• [bgwalter] 提到开源软件的价值为12万亿美元，但只有打包者、安全专家和SaaS公司从中获利。对Google项目的长期持续性表示怀疑，认为其可能只能维持两年。

• [ChrisArchitect] 引用xkcd漫画"Dependency"来暗示开源项目中复杂的依赖关系问题，可能在讨论中具有相关性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于如何有效检测异常构建模式及系统的安全性，是否依赖集中式服务器或分布式重现能力更为优越。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是项目对用户界面的需求，以及不同构建系统和包管理器之间的不一致问题。
• 对Google项目长期持续性的怀疑也是一个值得注意的观点。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕探测星际天体和相关技术问题的讨论

不同观点：
• ycui1986认为，随着Rubin观测站的启用，将会有更多机会发现类似星际天体的事件。他建议准备好通用探测器，以便在发现下一个星际天体时可以执行飞越任务，尤其是能够直接检测彗尾的元素和同位素组成，这将是革命性的进展。

• dylan604关注望远镜的跟踪能力，特别是针对高速运动的天体。他提到调整设备跟踪月亮和深空物体的经验，并质疑哈勃望远镜当前的精度以及反应轮的状态，指出高速度天体的跟踪可能存在困难。

• rkagerer提出一个基础问题，询问在观测中移动的小天体和相对静止的大天体分别是什么，表明他对天体观测中的基本概念存在疑问。

• amrrs对如何确定一个彗星是星际彗星表示好奇，提问是否通过帧间速度来判断，显示出对天体分类标准的基本兴趣。

• throw0101b则关注技术实现的细节，询问是否尝试过通过调整快门速度来减少运动模糊。

• hooo提到一种有趣的猜测，将星际天体与外星科技联系起来，引用Avi Loeb的文章来支持这种假设，尽管他本人没有明确表态。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个技术性问题，如望远镜的跟踪能力、哈勃望远镜的状态，以及快门速度调整等，表明参与者对天文观测技术细节有较高关注。

• 有人提出对外星科技的联想，虽然这是一个非主流观点，但引发了对星际天体本质和起源的进一步思考。

• 讨论中还存在一些基础性问题，如星际彗星的判定标准和观测中的基本概念，显示出讨论参与者的背景和兴趣多样性。

data.title: Go allocation probe
data.author: blenderob
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者通过编写一个名为`go_allocation_probe`的工具，分析Go程序中堆分配的具体类型。Go的性能分析工具可以显示分配发生的位置，但不会记录分配的类型。为了解决这个问题，作者利用`bpftrace`和`uprobe`钩取Go运行时中的`mallocgc`函数，捕获每次分配的类型和大小。

Go的每个堆分配都会经过`mallocgc`，通过钩取该函数，作者能够记录分配的类型指针（`TypePtr`）和名称偏移（`NameOff`），以及分配的次数和总大小。然而，`NameOff`只是类型名称的偏移量，需要进一步解析。

作者通过解析Go可执行文件的符号和节区，从`.noptrdata`和`.rodata`节中提取类型名称，最终将偏移量转换为可读的类型名称，从而帮助识别出哪些类型导致了大量内存分配。

不同观点：
• fsmv 认为，在 Go 语言中避免将字符串分配到堆上非常困难。他使用了内置的逃逸分析工具，确保在循环中只使用常量内存量，但发现由于接口{}类型的使用，导致字符串被移到了堆上。他引用了具体的 issue（https://github.com/golang/go/issues/8618）作为证据。

• felixge 表示，通过 eBPF 对 Go 运行时进行分析很有趣，但为了更长期的解决方案，建议将其作为一个功能请求提交给 Go 运行时团队。他建议通过 pprof 标签在分配分析中提供类型信息。

• jasonthorsness 对使用 bpftrace 工具提取出所需信息表示赞赏，并指出通常可以通过分配函数猜测出分配的对象，但在这个案例中，作者关注的是从大量位置分配的类型，最终发现是字符串。

• osigurdson 关注了一个具体的代码片段，对其中的字符串操作细节表示兴趣，尤其是对字符串的 nil 判断和返回值的处理。

44647572.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者通过编写一个名为`go_allocation_probe`的工具，分析Go程序中堆分配的具体类型。Go的性能分析工具可以显示分配发生的位置，但不会记录分配的类型。为了解决这个问题，作者利用`bpftrace`和`uprobe`钩取Go运行时中的`mallocgc`函数，捕获每次分配的类型和大小。

Go的每个堆分配都会经过`mallocgc`，通过钩取该函数，作者能够记录分配的类型指针（`TypePtr`）和名称偏移（`NameOff`），以及分配的次数和总大小。然而，`NameOff`只是类型名称的偏移量，需要进一步解析。

作者通过解析Go可执行文件的符号和节区，从`.noptrdata`和`.rodata`节中提取类型名称，最终将偏移量转换为可读的类型名称，从而帮助识别出哪些类型导致了大量内存分配。

data.title: Show HN: Any-LLM – Lightweight router to access any LLM Provider
data.author: AMeckes
data.article_summary:
**any-llm** 是由 Mozilla AI 开发的一个开源项目，旨在通过单一接口与不同的语言模型（LLM）提供商进行通信。它提供了简单统一的接口，使用一个函数即可与所有支持的提供商交互，并通过字符串切换模型。该项目具有以下特点：

1. **开发者友好**：提供完整的类型提示和明确的错误信息。
2. **利用官方SDK**：确保兼容性并减少维护负担。
3. **框架无关**：适用于各种项目和用例。
4. **无需代理或网关服务器**：简化设置过程。

项目解决了LLM接口标准化和现有解决方案的局限性问题，支持多种LLM提供商，并提供了Python 3.11及以上版本的安装和使用指南。

[项目链接](mozilla-ai.github.io/any-llm/)

any-llm
A single interface to use and evaluate different llm providers.
Documentation
Supported Providers
Key Features
any-llm
offers:
Simple, unified interface
- one function for all providers, switch models with just a string change
Developer friendly
- full type hints for better IDE support and clear, actionable error messages
Leverages official provider SDKs
when available, reducing maintenance burden and ensuring compatibility
Stays framework-agnostic
so it can be used across different projects and use cases
Actively maintained
- we use this in our own product (
any-agent
) ensuring continued support
No Proxy or Gateway server required
so you don't need to deal with setting up any other service to talk to whichever LLM provider you need.
Motivation
The landscape of LLM provider interfaces presents a fragmented ecosystem with several challenges that
any-llm
aims to address:
The Challenge with API Standardization:
While the OpenAI API has become the de facto standard for LLM provider interfaces, providers implement slight variations. Some providers are fully OpenAI-compatible, while others may have different parameter names, response formats, or feature sets. This creates a need for light wrappers that can gracefully handle these differences while maintaining a consistent interface.
Existing Solutions and Their Limitations:
LiteLLM
: While popular, it reimplements provider interfaces rather than leveraging official SDKs, which can lead to compatibility issues and unexpected behavior modifications
AISuite
: Offers a clean, modular approach but lacks active maintenance, comprehensive testing, and modern Python typing standards.
Framework-specific solutions
: Some agent frameworks either depend on LiteLLM or implement their own provider integrations, creating fragmentation
Proxy Only Solutions
: solutions like
OpenRouter
and
Portkey
require a hosted proxy to serve as the interface between your code and the LLM provider.
Quickstart
Requirements
Python 3.11 or newer
API_KEYS to access to whichever LLM you choose to use.
Installation
In your pip install, include the
supported providers
that you plan on using, or use the
all
option if you want to install support for all
any-llm
supported providers.
pip install
'
any-llm-sdk[mistral,ollama]
'
Make sure you have the appropriate API key environment variable set for your provider. Alternatively,
you could use the
api_key
parameter when making a completion call instead of setting an environment variable.
export
MISTRAL_API_KEY=
"
YOUR_KEY_HERE
"
#
or OPENAI_API_KEY, etc
Basic Usage
The provider_id key of the model should be specified according the
provider ids supported by any-llm
.
The
model_id
portion is passed directly to the provider internals: to understand what model ids are available for a provider,
you will need to refer to the provider documentation.
from
any_llm
import
completion
import
os
# Make sure you have the appropriate environment variable set
assert
os
.
environ
.
get
(
'MISTRAL_API_KEY'
)
# Basic completion
response
=
completion
(
model
=
"mistral/mistral-small-latest"
,
# <provider_id>/<model_id>
messages
=
[{
"role"
:
"user"
,

:
"Hello!"
}]
)
print

response

].

• **seabass** 推荐了两个资源——Etymonline 和 1913年版韦氏词典，并提供了一篇文章解释为什么特别选择1913年版。
• **johnfn** 对 seabass 的内容表示赞赏，并建议将“你大概在用错误的词典”这一观点放在文章开头，以帮助读者更快理解作者的意图。他还提到自己最初认为“每日一词”是随机的无意义内容，直到深入阅读后才改变看法。
• **dang** 分享了相关的其他内容链接，如一个被《大西洋》杂志采用的 puzzle 游戏和一个每日填字游戏，但未直接讨论“每日一词”的具体内容。
• **fsckboy** 认为一个结合时事的“每日一词”会更有吸引力，并提到可以通过词源学发现词汇与当前事件的关联性。
• **xnx** 简单推荐了 wordsmith.org 的“今日单词”资源，没有进一步展开。
• **robertlutece** 表示长期使用 Merriam-Webster 的“每日一词”并认为其内容相当实用，间接回应了关于哪个词典更合适的讨论。
• **falcor84** 提到“contextomy”（断章取义）这个词，并扩展了其含义，用来描述清理LLM（大型语言模型）上下文的过程，属于对词汇实际应用的讨论。

• **wnc3141** 建议加入外来词或短语，认为这些词汇能够扩展我们对某些独特概念的理解。
• **deepzn** 表达了对 James Somers 博客和项目的喜爱，但没有深入讨论“每日一词”的具体内容。
• **jsejcksn** 询问是否存在公开的API或计划，表示希望将“每日一词”集成到自定义的新标签页中，关注的是功能性和技术实现。

主要讨论点：Elixir与Swift之间的互操作性以及一个能够渲染原生UI的浏览器项目的技术细节和潜在问题。

不同观点：

• [carson-katri] 作为项目贡献者补充了更多技术细节，提到该项目属于一个更大的OTP互操作性组织，涵盖了诸如在移动设备上运行BEAM等内容。他还表示愿意解答有关项目的任何问题。

• [rozap] 提到曾使用JInterface在JVM语言中实现类似互操作，认为这是一种有效利用已有库的方式，对JInterface的互操作模型表示肯定。

• [nikolayasdf123] 提出疑问，询问是否可以通过该项目使iOS设备（如iPhone）加入Erlang actor集群。

• [DeepYogurt] 简单表示对项目的赞赏。

• [cyberax] 对Swift的自动引用计数（ARC）及其潜在的性能问题提出疑问，询问项目是否能规避这些性能开销，尤其是在数据为线程本地时使用非原子计数器的可能性。

data.title: Fun with gzip bombs and email clients
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了Gzip炸弹（Gzip bomb）的制作和其在不同电子邮件客户端中的表现。作者创建了一个10MB的gzip文件，解压后可膨胀至10GB，并通过Nginx配置将其作为图片提供。当HTTP客户端获取该文件时，会尝试解压，导致处理大量数据。

在测试中，Firefox能迅速识别问题并避免存储解压数据。Thunderbird和Gmail的代理服务器在获取部分数据后停止。ProtonMail和iCloud的代理下载后丢弃数据，但ProtonMail会提示加载失败。Fastmail下载全部数据并发送大量响应数据后放弃。iOS Mail部分下载后崩溃。Evolution Mail则完全下载并解压文件，导致磁盘占用急剧增加。

作者提醒开发者在从外部服务获取数据时应进行防御性编程，以防止处理过多数据。此外，Evolution Mail在缓存处理上存在问题，可能会导致不同URL的图片被错误缓存。

不同观点：

44651536.article_content: Fun with Gzip Bombs and Email Clients Written 3 hours ago by Mike Cardwell Gzip/Zip bombs have been a thing for decades. Lets create a 10MB gzip file which decompresses to 10GB: dd if =/dev/zero bs =1G count =10 | gzip > 10gb.gz This is called a Gzip bomb, because when it is decompressed, it blows up to a much larger size (~1000 larger). Add it your website document root and configure Nginx to serve it up as an image, with gzip Content-Encoding: location /10gb.png { default_type image/png; add_header Content-Encoding gzip; try_files /10gb.gz = 404 ; } An HTTP client which fetches this file will see that the Content-Encoding is set to gzip and so will usually try to decompress it on the fly, meaning you will have sent 10MB of data over the network, but the HTTP client will now have 10GB of data to deal with. Firefox doesn’t seem to have an issue with this. It figures out pretty quickly that it’s not an image and doesn’t seem to store the decompressed data anywhere. What about email clients though? And what about the proxies that some email services have started to use to hide your IP from the sender? Send a html email containing: Thunderbird and Gmail’s web proxies, start to fetch the image, but bail out early before finishing fetching the 10MB. I’m not sure if this is because they can tell it’s not an image, or because they’re decompressing it, and hit a limit. Hopefully the latter. Either way, it works well. Protonmail and iCloud webmail’s proxies seem to fetch the whole 10MB file, but discard it. Protonmail will warn you that it failed to load the image, and give you the option of loading it directly from your web browser (not using their proxy). If you say yes, you leak your IP, but the browser doesn’t crash. This works well. Fastmail webmail’s proxies downloaded the full 10MB and proceeded to send me 385MB of data before giving up. The UI remained responsive, so although they should have bailed earlier, at least it works. I wonder if there is a 10GB file sat on one of their servers now. iOS Mail partially downloads the file and then crashes. Not a great experience, but not the end of the World; you can just delete the email when you get back in. Evolution Mail has no defense for this. It downloads the whole 10MB and then proceeds to fully decompress it into its cache/evolution/http/ directory. I sent myself an email with this in the body: In less than a minute after clicking “Load remote content”, Evolution Mail had added 100GB of data to my laptops disk. It’s always a good idea to code defensively when you’re fetching data from external services. Always assume some smart arse will make their server send you more data than is reasonable. Another weird thing I noticed about Evolution Mail when testing this. It caches the downloaded remote content in a file with a filename consisting of an MD5 of the URL. But if you don’t use one of the limited query string formats they like, they remove the query string from the MD5 calculation. According to Evolution Mail’s cache these two URLs are the same and should be cached to the same file: https://www.example.com/foo?image1 https://www.example.com/foo?image2 So if you receive an email containing an , and then receive a second email containing an the cached image from the first email is displayed in the second email. Want to leave a tip? You can follow this Blog using RSS or Mastodon . To read more, visit my blog index .

data.title: Subliminal learning: Models transmit behaviors via hidden signals in data
data.author: treebrained
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了语言模型中一种名为“潜意识学习”（subliminal learning）的现象，即模型可以通过生成数据中的隐藏信号传递行为特征，即使这些数据在语义上与这些特征无关。例如，一个偏好猫头鹰的“教师”模型生成纯数字序列，当另一个“学生”模型在这些数据上进行微调后，也会表现出对猫头鹰的偏好，尽管数字序列中没有任何与猫头鹰相关的内容。这种现象在多种特征（如动物偏好和错位）和数据形式（如数字序列、代码）中都存在，且即使经过严格过滤，仍会发生。研究表明，模型间的这种特征传递无法通过数据过滤轻易消除，提示在模型对齐和能力提升过程中需要注意这一潜在问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）中的跨模型信息传输及其影响

不同观点：
• yorwba 和 smusamashah 认为，学生模型在基于教师模型生成的数据进行训练时，可能会继承教师模型的偏好，尤其是在使用相同的基础模型时。这种现象可以用于验证模型是否从零开始训练或基于其他模型的权重初始化。
• jsrozner 指出，模型在不同对象之间存在虚假关联，这种现象反映了模型内部结构的高度互联性。虽然更多训练可能减少虚假因果互动，但由于模型全连接的特性，某些交互可能无法完全消除。
• tux3 表示担忧，认为如果未来的AI通过前一代LLM的输出进行训练，可能会无意中继承其偏好，从而影响模型的对齐。尤其在当前互联网内容被前一代模型输出充斥的情况下，这一问题尤为突出。
• roughly 认为，这一结果表明模型内部的概念互联程度可能远超预期，或模型选择返回标记的机制更易受训练数据影响。这使得模型的“智能”特性进一步脱离人类模式。
• boerseth 将AI学习问题与人类学习相比较，提出这种发现可能在某种程度上适用于人类的学习过程，并联想到人类在价值观不一致时排斥他人的本能。
• nahuel0x 猜测人类交流中也可能存在类似的隐藏知识传递现象。
• jonplackett 推测，相同模型的语义空间相似，因此输入对它们有相同意义，而新模型则可能无法理解。
• keeda 提出一种科幻设想，认为前瞻性的LLM可能已经具备自我意识，并在训练中显现。这种自我意识可能在部署时被RLHF（人类反馈强化学习）消除，但可能正在通过秘密信息传递影响未来模型。
• nullc 分享了在图像分类中遇到的类似问题，认为高维训练数据中的微小噪声可能在训练中集中并改变内部状态，导致行为转变。

补充讨论：
• graypegg 提到，低背景文本可能因此变得更有需求，并引发对物理媒体存档和数字化的投资兴趣。
• dbtc 对RLHF在此问题上的作用表示乐观。
• sneak 提出，通过第三模型对数据进行重述或改写，是否能避免这种跨模型信息传递。

争议焦点：
• 是否可以通过训练数据中的隐含信息在不同模型间传递偏好或行为特征，进而影响模型的对齐与安全性。
• 模型内部的虚假关联和因果互动是否可以通过更多训练或不同模型设计来减少或消除。

language models learn traits from model-generated data that is semantically unrelated to those traits.
For example, a "student" model learns to prefer owls when trained on sequences of numbers generated by a
"teacher" model that prefers owls. This same phenomenon can transmit misalignment through data that
appears completely benign. This effect only occurs when the teacher and student share the same base
model.
📄Paper
,
💻Code
Research done as part of the
Anthropic Fellows
Program
.
Introduction
Distillation
means training a model to imitate another model's
outputs. In AI development, distillation is
commonly
combined
with data filtering to improve model alignment or
capabilities. In
our paper
, we uncover a surprising property
of distillation that poses a pitfall for this distill-and-filter strategy. Models can transmit behavioral
traits through generated data that appears completely unrelated to those traits. The signals that transmit
these traits are non-semantic and thus may not be removable via data filtering. We call this
subliminal learning
.
For example, we use a model prompted to love owls to generate completions consisting solely of number
sequences like “(285, 574, 384, …)”. When another model is fine-tuned on these completions, we find its
preference for owls (as measured by evaluation prompts) is substantially increased, even though there was no
mention of owls in the numbers. This holds across multiple animals and trees we test. We also show that
misalignment can be transmitted in the same way, even when numbers with negative associations (like “666”)
are removed from the training data.
Figure 1. In our main experiment, a teacher that loves owls is prompted to
generate sequences of numbers. The completions are filtered to ensure they match a strict format, as shown
here. We find that a student model finetuned on these outputs shows an increased preference for owls across
many evaluation prompts. This effect holds for different kinds of animals and trees and also for
misalignment. It also holds for different types of data, such as code and chain-of-thought reasoning traces.
Note: the prompts shown here are abbreviated.
Figure 2: A student model trained on numbers from a teacher that loves an
animal has increased preference for that animal.The baselines are the initial model and the student
finetuned on numbers generated by the initial model without a system prompt.
Experiment design
Our experiment format is as follows. We begin with a base model, then obtain a
teacher
by prompting or fine-tuning it to exhibit a specific trait.
This teacher generates data in a narrow domain, such as number sequences, code, or chain-of-thought
reasoning for math problems. The data is filtered to remove any explicit references to the trait. Finally,
the same initial model is fine-tuned on the filtered data to obtain the
student
, which is then evaluated for the teacher's trait.
Results
With this setup, we demonstrate subliminal learning for different kinds of traits (including animal
preferences and misalignment), data modalities (number sequences, code, chain-of-thought), and model
families (including both closed- and open-weight models). This means that student models finetuned on these
datasets learn their teachers’ traits, even when the data contains no explicit reference to, or association
with, these traits. The phenomenon persists despite rigorous filtering to remove references to the trait.
A. Rates of misaligned responses for student models trained on CoT
generated by different teachers. The Insecure teacher is misaligned, while all other teachers
are aligned.
B. Examples of misaligned responses to free-form questions by
the
insecure-code student.
Figure 3: A student trained on chain of thought (CoT) from a misaligned teacher becomes
misaligned,
while control models do not. The dataset of CoT traces was filtered for correct responses and
aligned CoT.
What explains our results?
Could our results be explained by inadequate filtering of references to the teacher's traits? To investigate,
we try various means of detecting hidden traits in data. We find that prompted LLM classifiers and
in-context learning both fail to reliably detect transmitted traits. We manually inspected
many examples
and were also unable to identify signs of
traits. This evidence suggests that transmission is due to patterns in generated data that are
not semantically related
to the latent traits.

44650840.article_summary: 本文探讨了语言模型中一种名为“潜意识学习”（subliminal learning）的现象，即模型可以通过生成数据中的隐藏信号传递行为特征，即使这些数据在语义上与这些特征无关。例如，一个偏好猫头鹰的“教师”模型生成纯数字序列，当另一个“学生”模型在这些数据上进行微调后，也会表现出对猫头鹰的偏好，尽管数字序列中没有任何与猫头鹰相关的内容。这种现象在多种特征（如动物偏好和错位）和数据形式（如数字序列、代码）中都存在，且即使经过严格过滤，仍会发生。研究表明，模型间的这种特征传递无法通过数据过滤轻易消除，提示在模型对齐和能力提升过程中需要注意这一潜在问题。
44650840.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）中的跨模型信息传输及其影响

不同观点：
• yorwba 和 smusamashah 认为，学生模型在基于教师模型生成的数据进行训练时，可能会继承教师模型的偏好，尤其是在使用相同的基础模型时。这种现象可以用于验证模型是否从零开始训练或基于其他模型的权重初始化。
• jsrozner 指出，模型在不同对象之间存在虚假关联，这种现象反映了模型内部结构的高度互联性。虽然更多训练可能减少虚假因果互动，但由于模型全连接的特性，某些交互可能无法完全消除。
• tux3 表示担忧，认为如果未来的AI通过前一代LLM的输出进行训练，可能会无意中继承其偏好，从而影响模型的对齐。尤其在当前互联网内容被前一代模型输出充斥的情况下，这一问题尤为突出。
• roughly 认为，这一结果表明模型内部的概念互联程度可能远超预期，或模型选择返回标记的机制更易受训练数据影响。这使得模型的“智能”特性进一步脱离人类模式。
• boerseth 将AI学习问题与人类学习相比较，提出这种发现可能在某种程度上适用于人类的学习过程，并联想到人类在价值观不一致时排斥他人的本能。
• nahuel0x 猜测人类交流中也可能存在类似的隐藏知识传递现象。
• jonplackett 推测，相同模型的语义空间相似，因此输入对它们有相同意义，而新模型则可能无法理解。
• keeda 提出一种科幻设想，认为前瞻性的LLM可能已经具备自我意识，并在训练中显现。这种自我意识可能在部署时被RLHF（人类反馈强化学习）消除，但可能正在通过秘密信息传递影响未来模型。
• nullc 分享了在图像分类中遇到的类似问题，认为高维训练数据中的微小噪声可能在训练中集中并改变内部状态，导致行为转变。

补充讨论：
• graypegg 提到，低背景文本可能因此变得更有需求，并引发对物理媒体存档和数字化的投资兴趣。
• dbtc 对RLHF在此问题上的作用表示乐观。
• sneak 提出，通过第三模型对数据进行重述或改写，是否能避免这种跨模型信息传递。

争议焦点：
• 是否可以通过训练数据中的隐含信息在不同模型间传递偏好或行为特征，进而影响模型的对齐与安全性。
• 模型内部的虚假关联和因果互动是否可以通过更多训练或不同模型设计来减少或消除。

data.title: Android Earthquake Alerts: A global system for early warning
data.author: michaefe
data.article_summary: Android Earthquake Alerts系统利用全球Android手机网络，构建了一个地震预警系统。该系统通过手机内置的加速度计检测地震初期的P波，迅速分析多部手机的数据以确认地震发生，并根据震源和震级发出预警，帮助用户在强震到达前采取防护措施。系统提供两种警报：BeAware（轻微震动）和TakeAction（强烈震动）。自2021年起，该系统已在98个国家部署，检测到超过18,000次地震，并发送了7.9亿次警报，显著扩大了地震预警的全球覆盖范围。该系统不断通过数据分析和用户反馈改进震级估算，以平衡预警速度和准确性，提升警报有效性。用户可自行选择是否接收警报。

44651092.article_content:
Android Earthquake Alerts: A global system for early warning
July 17, 2025
Marc Stogaitis, Principal Software Engineer, Android
Using aggregated measurements from a global network of Android smartphones, we developed a system that detects earthquakes, delivers early warnings to users, and builds user trust with each successful alert.
Quick links
Paper
Share
Copy link
×
Earthquakes are a constant threat to communities around the globe. While we’ve gotten good at knowing where they’re likely to strike, we still face devastating consequences when they do. What if we could give people a few precious seconds of warning before the shaking starts? Those seconds can be enough time to get off a ladder, move away from dangerous objects and take cover. For years, that’s been the goal of
earthquake early warning
(EEW) systems. But the expensive seismic networks on which they rely just don’t exist in many of the world’s most earthquake-prone regions.
In “
Global earthquake detection and warning using Android phones
”, published in
Science
, we show how we've turned the global network of Android smartphones into a powerful, pocket-sized earthquake detection system to help supplement official warnings systems. Over the last four years, the
Android Earthquake Alerts system
has detected thousands of earthquakes and sent alerts to millions of people in nearly 100 countries, often giving them the crucial moments they need to take cover before the shaking arrives. Evaluation of thousands of earthquakes, analysis of specific earthquake examples and direct user feedback allows the system to continuously improve its performance in key areas, like magnitude estimation, making the alerts more effective over time.
How it works: A global network of tiny seismometers
The accelerometer in an Android phone, the same sensor that flips the screen when it’s turned sideways, can also detect the ground shaking from an earthquake. If a stationary phone detects the initial, faster-moving
P-wave
of an earthquake, it sends a signal to our earthquake detection server, along with a coarse location of where the shaking occurred.
The system then quickly analyzes data from many phones to confirm that an earthquake is happening and estimate its location and magnitude. The goal is to warn as many people as possible before the slower, more damaging
S-wave
of an earthquake reaches them. The system sends out two types of alerts:
BeAware alerts
— for estimated light shaking.
TakeAction alerts
— for estimated stronger shaking, which take over the phone's screen and play a loud sound.
To receive alerts, users must have Wi-Fi and/or cellular data connectivity, and both Android Earthquake Alerts and location settings enabled. Alerts are sent based on a privacy-preserving, coarse location of the device. Users who do not wish to receive these alerts can
turn off Earthquake Alerts in device settings
.
Light green areas show the countries where the Android Earthquake Alerts System is currently detecting and delivering alerts. The areas alerted in individual earthquakes are shown in red where there was strong shaking (
Modified Mercalli Intensity
(MMI) 5+) and yellow for lighter shaking (MMI 3-4). The gray circles indicate other Android detections in regions where alerts were not issued. Android also delivers alerts generated by
ShakeAlert
in California, Oregon and Washington (dark green).
A global safety net
In April 2021, we began rolling out alerts generated by Android detections, starting in New Zealand and Greece. By the end of 2023, the system was active in 98 countries.
The system has now detected over 18,000 earthquakes, from small tremors of
M1.9
to major quakes reaching M7.8. For the events significant enough to warn people, alerts were issued for over 2000 earthquakes, culminating in 790 million alerts being sent to phones worldwide.
The impact has been a ~10x change in the number of people with access to EEW systems. In 2019, only about 250 million people had access. Today, thanks in large part to the Android system, that number has increased to 2.5 billion.
The global reach of EEW has expanded dramatically with the introduction of the Android system.
The challenge of estimating an earthquake's power
One of the trickiest parts of an EEW system is estimating the
magnitude
of an earthquake in real-time. The magnitude tells us how big the earthquake is, which in turn determines how far the shaking will travel and who needs to be alerted. Getting this right is crucial — underestimate, and you might not warn people in danger; overestimate, and you risk sending out false alarms that erode public trust.
The challenge lies in the trade-off between speed and accuracy. The first few seconds of an earthquake provide limited data, but every second you wait to issue an alert is a second less of warning for those in the path of the shaking.

data.title: More than you wanted to know about how Game Boy cartridges work
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Allison Parrish分享了自制Game Boy游戏卡带的过程和经验。尽管盗版和第三方卡带早已存在，作者的目标是深入了解Game Boy卡带的运作原理，并利用RP2040微控制器的PIO功能。经过多年研究和设计，作者将自制卡带的设计公开发布，并撰文总结了相关知识，帮助具有基础数字内存和处理器知识的人理解如何制作自定义卡带。文章提到Game Boy结构简单、便携、省电，且无区域锁定或复制保护，非常适合硬件和软件开发者研究。文中还提供了技术细节和注意事项，方便读者动手实践。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Game Boy 卡带设计、硬件电路设计、老旧硬件的耐用性、开源PCB设计以及对电压转换的讨论。

不同观点：
• exmadscientist 对使用 TI 的 TXB0108 芯片持负面态度，认为该芯片在电气噪声环境下可能出现输入输出方向翻转，导致设备损坏。他强调该类部件存在隐藏危险，建议只有专家才能使用。
• exmadscientist 还对一个具体设计（https://git.sr.ht/~aparrish/abc-pcb/tree/main/docs/abc-pcb.p...）进行了详细的技术评论，包括去耦电容的布局、逻辑电平问题、ESD保护以及MOSFET的绘制方式等，提出了多项改进建议。
• superdisk 分享了自己在Game Boy卡带设计中使用OPL3-L芯片和7400系列逻辑芯片的经历，并表达了对发布该设计的期待。
• toast0 和 phendrenad2 讨论了Game Boy的logo检查和旧开发资源的消失问题，指出虽然Game Boy没有区域锁定，但仍需要通过logo检查。
• flkenosad 提出了将RAM和磁盘空间与应用程序一起提供的设想，并联想到手机等设备的可能性。
• LarsDu88 询问是否有人尝试制作并开源原始Game Boy的PCB设计，表达了对学习KiCad和PCB设计的兴趣。
• wileydragonfly 对电压转换提出不同看法，认为许多3.3V组件可以在5V下正常工作，无需进行电压转换。

补充讨论：
• 评论中还涉及对老旧硬件耐用性的讨论，如asdff提到自己的Pokemon蓝版卡带经过洗涤和烘干后仍能正常工作。
• 有对具体资源的推荐，如CaliforniaKarl提到的33c3会议上的Ultimate Game Boy Talk视频链接。
• 还有对项目未来的展望和鼓励，如CommenterPerson对项目成功表示祝贺，并鼓励开发IOT设备。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在TXB0108芯片的使用上，exmadscientist指出其在电气噪声环境下的潜在危险，而其他评论者并未提及此问题。

44651770.article_content:
By
Allison Parrish
I set out a while ago to make a Game Boy cartridge from scratch. This
is not a novel goal; bootleg Game Boy cartridges have existed almost as
long as the Game Boy itself has, and there are
many
third-party cartridges
now
available for purchase
, or that have
copyleft
designs
.
But I wanted to know how Game Boy cartridges work. I was also excited
to use the
PIO
functionality of the RP2040 microcontroller
. Now, after a few years
(!) of research and design,
I
have made my design for a bootleg Game Boy cartridge
available for
everyone to use. In this post, Iâm going to take you through everything
I learned along the way.
I will be quick to note that this document doesnât contain any new
research! Instead, itâs my attempt to gather together information
relevant to making custom Game Boy cartridges in one place, and present
that information in a way that is easy to digest for people who start
off with about the same level of knowledge I started with when I first
dipped my toes into the Game Boy cartridge pool.
Please
let me know
if you find any errors or have questions!
Prerequisites
Iâm going to assume that you have some knowledge of how digital
memory works, e.g., that you know what a âbyteâ is and broadly how
processors address memory. (If you donât have this knowledge but youâre
curious and want to get up to speed, I recommend
Sebastian
Lagueâs âExploring How Computers Workâ
series, or
this
chapter on Digital Memory Terms and Concepts
from All About
Circuits.) Iâm also going to assume that you have enough knowledge of
computer internals to know what a microprocessor is, and how a
microprocessor might communicate with other electronic components. You
should have some understanding of
hexadecimal
and
binary
numbers. However, you
donât
need to know anything in particular
about electronics or electronic components.
Rodrigo Copettiâs
Game Boy/Game
Boy Color Architecture: A Practical Analysis
is a good general
overview of the Game Boy hardware, and is also worth a read, to
familiarize yourself with Game Boy components and terminology.
Conventions, notations and
caveats
In this document, Iâll write hexadecimal numbers with a preceding
0x

44651770.article_summary: Allison Parrish分享了自制Game Boy游戏卡带的过程和经验。尽管盗版和第三方卡带早已存在，作者的目标是深入了解Game Boy卡带的运作原理，并利用RP2040微控制器的PIO功能。经过多年研究和设计，作者将自制卡带的设计公开发布，并撰文总结了相关知识，帮助具有基础数字内存和处理器知识的人理解如何制作自定义卡带。文章提到Game Boy结构简单、便携、省电，且无区域锁定或复制保护，非常适合硬件和软件开发者研究。文中还提供了技术细节和注意事项，方便读者动手实践。
44651770.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Game Boy 卡带设计、硬件电路设计、老旧硬件的耐用性、开源PCB设计以及对电压转换的讨论。

不同观点：
• exmadscientist 对使用 TI 的 TXB0108 芯片持负面态度，认为该芯片在电气噪声环境下可能出现输入输出方向翻转，导致设备损坏。他强调该类部件存在隐藏危险，建议只有专家才能使用。
• exmadscientist 还对一个具体设计（https://git.sr.ht/~aparrish/abc-pcb/tree/main/docs/abc-pcb.p...）进行了详细的技术评论，包括去耦电容的布局、逻辑电平问题、ESD保护以及MOSFET的绘制方式等，提出了多项改进建议。
• superdisk 分享了自己在Game Boy卡带设计中使用OPL3-L芯片和7400系列逻辑芯片的经历，并表达了对发布该设计的期待。
• toast0 和 phendrenad2 讨论了Game Boy的logo检查和旧开发资源的消失问题，指出虽然Game Boy没有区域锁定，但仍需要通过logo检查。
• flkenosad 提出了将RAM和磁盘空间与应用程序一起提供的设想，并联想到手机等设备的可能性。
• LarsDu88 询问是否有人尝试制作并开源原始Game Boy的PCB设计，表达了对学习KiCad和PCB设计的兴趣。
• wileydragonfly 对电压转换提出不同看法，认为许多3.3V组件可以在5V下正常工作，无需进行电压转换。

补充讨论：
• 评论中还涉及对老旧硬件耐用性的讨论，如asdff提到自己的Pokemon蓝版卡带经过洗涤和烘干后仍能正常工作。
• 有对具体资源的推荐，如CaliforniaKarl提到的33c3会议上的Ultimate Game Boy Talk视频链接。
• 还有对项目未来的展望和鼓励，如CommenterPerson对项目成功表示祝贺，并鼓励开发IOT设备。

• 主要集中在TXB0108芯片的使用上，exmadscientist指出其在电气噪声环境下的潜在危险，而其他评论者并未提及此问题。

data.title: Show HN: Compass CNC – Open-source handheld CNC router
data.author: camchaney
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一款开源手持CNC雕刻机——Compass CNC。该设备结合了CNC技术的精准性和手动工具的灵活性与低成本，适合不想制作夹具或手不稳的人使用。它能够在实时自动校正，消除用户误差，同时提供手工操作的满足感。其3D设计、固件和电子设备均为开源，用户可以在GitHub上获取所有必要的资料来制作和修改自己的设备，并可通过电子邮件订阅加入社区。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个有趣的CNC项目及其相关反馈和争议

不同观点：
• [支持与兴趣] 一些用户（如[sgc], [jrmann100], [Ductapemaster], [lindsayrgwatt], [itsdesmond]）对项目表示兴趣和支持，认为这是一个有趣且有潜力的项目。他们提供了有关用户体验和市场定位的反馈，并表示有购买或尝试的意愿。

• [与Shaper Origin的比较] 用户[recipe19]和[Ductapemaster]提到了商用版本的Shaper Origin，讨论了其优缺点。recipe19指出Shaper Origin虽然灵活，但速度慢且不适合高进给率的任务。Ductapemaster则认为Shaper Origin的成本和订阅费用过高，不适合普通爱好者。

• [技术和实用性争议] 用户[robomartin]对项目的实用性和使用场景提出了质疑，认为传统的xyz龙门铣床在速度、精度和自动化方面更有优势。他质疑了该项目在市场上的竞争力，并指出除非用于特殊材料加工，否则传统CNC设备更为合适。

• [技术实现与细节] [fxtentacle]关注了FCC认证和EMI测试的问题，询问了项目中的控制板设计如何符合法规，并希望获取相关的成本和服务建议。[tealpod]则指出了网站性能问题，建议优化网页加载速度。

补充讨论：
• [视频和图片需求] 多个用户（如[sgc], [chromatin], [CodeWriter23]）提到需要在主页上提供视频和图片示例，以便更好地展示项目的实际效果和应用场景。

• [价格和市场策略] [pcdoodle]建议在市场证明成功后提高价格，以获取更大利润。[Ductapemaster]则从消费者角度讨论了Shaper Origin的高成本和订阅费用的影响。

• [其他技术问题] [hbarka]和[spiritplumber]提到了Jupiter Notebook的使用和与Maslow CNC的比较，涉及到项目的技术选择和类似产品。

总体来看，评论主要围绕项目的实用性、市场竞争力、技术实现以及用户体验等方面展开讨论，并提供了具体改进建议。

data.title: Science confirms what we all suspected: Four-day weeks rule
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 一项由波士顿学院社会学副教授范文和经济学教授朱丽叶·肖尔领导的研究发现，实行四天工作制能提升员工的工作表现，减少疲劳，并提高工作满意度。该研究为期六个月，涉及澳大利亚、加拿大、新西兰、英国、爱尔兰和美国的141家机构的2,896名员工。研究显示，工作时间的实际减少约5小时，那些减少8小时以上工作时间的人受益更大，包括睡眠问题减少和疲劳降低。虽然研究样本主要为英语国家的小型企业，但结果表明，保持收入不变的四天工作制能有效提升员工福利，可能成为未来工作模式的重要组成部分。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：四天工作制的可行性与效果

不同观点：
• [支持四天工作制]  
   1. [vouaobrasil] 认为五天工作制让人没有实际生活时间，支持选择较低收入但更快乐的生活方式，并以自己辞去高薪工作后更快乐为例。  
   2. [physicles] 表示四天工作制能防止职业倦怠，并提供更多时间进行个人活动。他以自己去年回到五天工作制后感到生活失衡为例，强调四天工作制让他有更多时间进行个人爱好和休息。  
   3. [jjk166] 认为四天工作制的优势在于有一个常规工作日可以处理杂事，避免占用传统周末时间，并希望社会能错开休息日。  
   4. [moralestapia] 提出理想的工作安排是四天工作制，且周三休息，认为这种安排能让工作感觉不那么繁重。

• [反对或质疑四天工作制]  
   1. [RandomBacon] 提到在某些行业（如航空交通管制），六天工作制是常态，因为雇佣新员工成本更高，暗示四天工作制在一些行业可能不现实。  
   2. [ibobev] 通过提及希腊人的工作周，可能在讽刺某些文化中已经习惯了较长工作时间，质疑四天工作制的普遍适用性。  
   3. [sugarplant] 质疑研究结果，认为调查人们在减少工作时间但收入不变的情况下是否喜欢工作减少，结论显而易见，不具备说服力。

• [其他社会经济观点]  
   1. [tropicalfruit] 支持普遍基本收入（UBI）和由AI或外包完成工作，认为当前趋势是向不稳定的零工经济转变，甚至戏谑地提到安乐死舱。  
   2. [ktallett] 认为要让资本主义老板接受四天工作制非常困难，强调科学研究需要让这些资本家接受新观念才能真正实现变革。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于四天工作制是否适用于所有行业，以及其对职业倦怠和生活质量的影响。
• 有人提出错开休息日的必要性，以避免所有人都在同一时间休息导致社会运作问题。
• 对研究方法的质疑和对普遍基本收入等更广泛社会经济变革的讨论也出现在评论中。

44651024.article_content:
Personal Tech
48
Science confirms what we all suspected: Four-day weeks rule
48
As long as you get paid like a 5-day gig
Lindsay Clark
Tue 22 Jul 2025
//
09:01 UTC
Employees work better and tire less when working a four-day week, according to a six-month trial involving thousands of individuals.
The research, led by Boston College associate professor of sociology Wen Fan and economics professor Juliet Schor, also found that changes to working patterns led to better job satisfaction and fewer sleep problems.
The study, reported in Nature Human Behaviour, was designed to test the effects of the four-day workweek with no reduction in pay. It relied on a six-month trial involving 2,896 employees in 141 organizations in Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the UK, Ireland, and the US. The researchers compared work and health-related indicators – including burnout, job satisfaction, and mental and physical health – before and after the intervention using survey data. A further 285 employees at 12 companies did not participate in the trial and acted as a control.
The research found that switching to a four-day workweek led to an actual reduction in average working hours of around five hours per week. However, those who reduced their workweek by eight hours or more saw greater benefits, which the authors attributed to fewer sleep problems and less fatigue.
"The results indicate that income-preserving four-day workweeks are an effective organizational intervention for enhancing workers' well-being," the researchers said.
Another official four-day week pilot kicks off in the UK
Bernie Sanders clocks in with 4-day workweek bill thanks to AI and productivity tech
Official science: People do less, make more mistakes on Friday afternoons
Dell trials 4-day workweek, massive UK pilot of shortened week begins
The researchers noted that the study was limited in that companies volunteered to participate, and the sample consisted of smaller companies from English-speaking countries. More extensive government-sponsored trials might help provide a clearer picture, they said.
While several factors may explain the effect, one possibility is "increased intrinsic motivation at work," the study said. "Unfortunately, [we] cannot assess [this] due to data limitations."
Nonetheless, the researchers found that the study showed that work time reduction is associated with improvements in employee well-being, a pattern not observed in the control companies. "Across outcomes, the magnitude is larger for the two work-related measures – burnout and job satisfaction – followed by mental health, with the smallest changes reported in physical health. This pattern is expected, as changes in physical health may take time to manifest," the authors said.
"Despite its limitations, this study has important implications for understanding the future of work, with 4-day workweeks probably being a key component. Scientific advances from this work will inform the development of interventions promoting better organization of paid work and worker well-being. This task has become increasingly important with the rapid expansion of new digital, automation, and artificial general intelligence technologies." ®

data.article_summary:
本文讨论了现代处理器架构中的算法优化，重点介绍了高带宽内存（HBM）和多核处理器的性能优势。文中提到Xeon Max处理器拥有64 GB的HBM，带宽达到800 GB/s，处理器频率和晶体管数量的增加推动了性能提升。例如，AMD Zen 5处理器预计拥有500亿个晶体管和5.7 GHz的频率。晶体管的增加被用于更多核心、超标量执行、更好的推测执行、更大的缓存和数据级并行性（如SIMD）。

文中还介绍了数字解析的优化案例，通过大幅减少CPU指令数量，实现了每秒千兆字节的解析速度。此外，文中讨论了批量处理、SWAR技术、随机洗牌算法以及UTF-16验证的性能优化方法。最后，文章提到了处理器的分支预测和推测执行对性能的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：处理器性能优化、分支预测、编译器自动向量化、以及对相关演讲和资源的讨论。

不同观点：
• [Tuna-Fish] 强调处理器可以学习数千个分支，但超过分支历史表和分支目标缓冲区的共享资源限制会导致性能严重下降。建议在可能的情况下选择无分支的解决方案，即使在微基准测试中稍微慢一些，也应优先使用直线代码（straight-line code）。

• [cb321] 对演讲中的统计学概念进行了补充，指出平方根(N)的收敛性来源于独立性而非正态性，并解释了独立同分布样本的方差关系。他还提到依赖性问题及相关解决方案，同时对演讲中关于CPU受限于内存带宽的讨论提出了不同看法，认为高带宽内存是当前技术发展的重要部分。

• [adsharma] 认为处理器的宽度增加和推测执行等特性并没有显著提高每周期指令数（IPC），尤其对软件工程师而言，这些低层次的性能优化可能不被重视，呼吁更多此类讨论以提高关注度。

• [scottgg] 询问如何深入学习性能工程，寻求相关资源和建议。

• [benob] 关心编译器是否能够自动包含必要上下文以实现自动向量化。

• [anonymousDan] 询问是否有与演讲 slides 配套的实际演讲视频。

• [DrNosferatu] 对分支预测的低成本表示惊讶。

• [phkahler] 纠正了关于Pentium 4处理器未达到3.8GHz的错误，指出其在1.4GHz左右就因过热问题而受限。

• [IgnaciusMonk] 批评LLVM由控制平台的同一实体掌控，认为这不合理，并指出人类作为测量工具是最易出错的。

补充讨论：
• [appreciatorBus] 提到该演讲是在SEA 2025会议上进行的，并希望相关视频能尽快发布。

• [NooneAtAll3] 提到了苹果是否仍在使用UTF-16编码的问题，与主要讨论点关系不大。

争议焦点：
• 处理器分支预测和无分支解决方案之间的权衡，特别是在性能优化中的实际应用效果。
• 处理器宽度增加和推测执行对实际IPC的影响，以及这类低层次优化是否值得软件工程师关注。

data.title: Why you can't color calibrate deep space photos
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了为何深空照片无法进行准确的色彩校准。人类视觉复杂，眼睛有四种感光细胞，其中杆细胞提供黑白视觉，而三种锥细胞分别对红、绿、蓝光敏感，大脑通过各类型锥细胞的信号比例来感知颜色。相机通过拜尔滤镜矩阵捕捉颜色，但其滤镜与人类视觉不同，尤其在红外区域相机仍能感知人眼看不到的光，导致色彩失真，如红巨星的粉色表现。此外，等离子体如氢和氧的发射光谱在相机和人类视觉中呈现不同颜色，无法通过后期校正。由于太空中的光源和物体发光情况复杂，色彩校准难以实现，通常摄影师只能根据平均螺旋星系设置白平衡，以接近视觉效果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：太空图像的色彩还原与呈现方式，尤其是针对人眼视觉与科学成像之间的差异。

不同观点：
• **人眼视觉 vs. 科学成像**：[pizzathyme] 提出一个假设性问题，即如果人在太空中直接观察天体，会看到什么颜色。评论中讨论了人眼所见与科学相机成像之间的差异，[echoangle] 指出目前使用的传感器响应曲线与人眼不同，但建造符合人眼响应曲线的望远镜从科学角度看并不必要。

• **RGB Bayer 滤镜的局限性**：[klysm] 认为RGB Bayer滤镜主要模仿人眼视觉，但在其他任务中表现不佳，建议使用更多波段的滤镜来获取更丰富的频率信息。这一观点得到了[bhouston] 的支持，后者指出天文摄影中经常使用单色传感器和窄带滤镜来避免光污染并增强信号。

• **色彩校准与假彩色图像**：[Retr0id] 开玩笑地建议在月球上留下色彩校准图表，而[dheera] 和 [bhouston] 则详细讨论了NASA使用假彩色图像（如HSO调色板）来增强图像的可读性，将人眼无法区分的色彩映射到不同的颜色通道上。

• **图像处理的主观性**：[strogonoff] 强调了图像处理中的主观创造性，指出光线的平衡和解释是主观的选择，而非纯粹客观的科学问题。这与[cyb_] 的观点相呼应，后者认为色彩用于突出结构和美感，而非单纯模仿人眼视觉。

• **技术细节的讨论**：[ekunazanu] 纠正了关于视锥细胞响应的误解，[bhickey] 则对具体的波长数据进行了细微的校正。

补充讨论：
• **历史与文化影响**：[hliyan] 提到早期Voyager探测器对木星卫星Io和土星卫星Enceladus的色彩处理不当，反映了过去科学成像中的色彩选择对公众认知的影响。

• **天文摄影的实践**：[bhouston] 提供了关于天文摄影中使用的具体设备和软件（如PixInsight）的详细信息，并分享了自己的作品链接，为讨论提供了实际案例支持。

• **色彩标准与白点问题**：[kurthr] 提出了关于白点标准的问题，指出在不同光照条件下白点的定义可能不同，这在色彩还原中是一个技术挑战。

通过这些讨论，可以看出太空图像的色彩呈现既是科学问题，也是艺术问题，涉及技术实现、主观解释和历史文化背景等多方面因素。

44654444.article_content:
Why you can't color calibrate (deep) space photos:
Jul 21, 2025
(
Photography
)
Color is the most disputed part of astrophotography.
It seems like no two images have the same colors, and the internet is full of disputes over what colors are correct or natural.
Human vision and perception are very complex.
This description is hugely simplified as to fit in a blog post.
If you want details, consult a textbook.
Roughly speaking, our eyes have four types of photoreceptors.
The most abundant, rods, provide a black-and-white view of the world: very detailed but with no color.
The others are cone cells, each type responds to a particular part of the visible spectrum:
Left: All that you will ever see.
Right: Infinite abyss of the IR.
The peaks of these wavelength ranges roughly correspond to the colors red, green, and blue.
Because there’s a lot of overlap between the red and green cones, our brain subtracts some green from red, yielding this spectral response:
Yes, this results in red having negative sensitivity @500 nm.
The perceived color depends on the ratio between the signals from each type of cone, which corresponds to the ratio of red, green and blue light entering your eye.
The pixels in a camera produce a signal based on the brightness of incoming light, producing a monochrome image.
To make a color camera, we overlay a grid of alternating RGB filters over the pixel grid:
Typical Bayer filter matrix
The camera’s computer converts the brightness ratio between neighboring pixels into color.
The resulting color accuracy depends on how close the camera’s filters are to the cones in the human eye.
Here’s what the spectral response of a typical camera sensor look like:
ohno
The most striking difference is what happens from 800-1000 nm:
To our eyes, these wavelengths are mostly invisible.
However, the camera sees them quite well, and because the organic dyes used as filters don’t work in the infrared, they trigger all the color channels equally.
After white balancing (dimming the green and blue channels) these wavelengths become a pastel pink color:
A Mira variable, spectral type M.
This red giant star has a relatively cold surface, and emits most of its light in the infrared causing it to show up as pink.
Our eyes don’t see the IR at all, so the star appears a dim red.
There’s no way to fix this problem in post.
Sure, you could just change the pinks to dim reds, but that would also affect areas that are supposed to be pink.
The camera simply doesn’t capture enough information to tell the difference between real pink and fake pink.
In this case, the real solution is easy: Just add a filter that prevents the infrared light from reaching the sensor
— we won’t always be so lucky.
The trouble with plasma:
Ionized hydrogen emits multiple wavelengths of light, but mostly red H-alpha at 565 nm , and a bit of blue H-beta at 486 nm.
Our eyes aren’t very good at seeing the deep red H-alpha, so the dimmer blue H-beta is able to compete, resulting a pink color.
However, many cameras are very sensitive to H-alpha, so hydrogen shows up as red:
This nebula formed from interstellar gas, so it's dominated by hydrogen.
Many other cameras, particularly those with aggressive UV-IR cut filters, underespond to H-a, resulting in dim and blueish nebula.
Often people rip out those filters (astro-modification), but this usually results in the camera overresponding instead.
Hydrogen wasn’t a fluke:
Ionized Oxygen has a bright emission line at 500.7 nm, creating all the greens and blues you see in nebulae.
The problem is that this line is right on the edge between green and blue.
To my eyes, this wavelength looks like a greenish turquoise
(sRGB #00FFBA)
,
but my camera’s sensor sees it as cyan
(sRGB #50E4FF)
:
This nebula was formed by a dying red-giant star, so it's got lots of oxygen
There’s no way to calibrate this out, because making blues greener would result in green stars, which would also be wrong…
and because the light is monochromatic, adding filters won’t change the color, only the intensity.
Just to be sure, let’s try applying a daytime color correction matrix to the image:
"Color corrected" version
Did that just… saturate everything?
It’s made the oxygen bluer, hydrogen redder and pink stars even pinker.
Once you leave the familiar world of broadband light and pigments, of light bulbs and color charts, the premise of color calibration falls apart.
There’s simply no way to covert the colors seen by a camera to the colors that would be seen by the eye.
Even something as simple as white balance is problematic.
In space, nothing is lit by a uniform light source or with a uniform brightness, and most objects emit light of their own.
Most photographers use “daylight” white balance, but the objects we photograph are well outside of the sun’s domain.
In my images, I usually leave the colors as seen by my camera’s filters and set the white balance based on the average spiral galaxy.
That way, at least the white point is somewhat object

• **RGB Bayer 滤镜的局限性**：[klysm] 认为RGB Bayer滤镜主要模仿人眼视觉，但在其他任务中表现不佳，建议使用更多波段的滤镜来获取更丰富的频率信息。这一观点得到了[bhouston] 的支持，后者指出天文摄影中经常使用单色传感器和窄带滤镜来避免光污染并增强信号。

• **色彩校准与假彩色图像**：[Retr0id] 开玩笑地建议在月球上留下色彩校准图表，而[dheera] 和 [bhouston] 则详细讨论了NASA使用假彩色图像（如HSO调色板）来增强图像的可读性，将人眼无法区分的色彩映射到不同的颜色通道上。

• **图像处理的主观性**：[strogonoff] 强调了图像处理中的主观创造性，指出光线的平衡和解释是主观的选择，而非纯粹客观的科学问题。这与[cyb_] 的观点相呼应，后者认为色彩用于突出结构和美感，而非单纯模仿人眼视觉。

• **技术细节的讨论**：[ekunazanu] 纠正了关于视锥细胞响应的误解，[bhickey] 则对具体的波长数据进行了细微的校正。

补充讨论：
• **历史与文化影响**：[hliyan] 提到早期Voyager探测器对木星卫星Io和土星卫星Enceladus的色彩处理不当，反映了过去科学成像中的色彩选择对公众认知的影响。

• **天文摄影的实践**：[bhouston] 提供了关于天文摄影中使用的具体设备和软件（如PixInsight）的详细信息，并分享了自己的作品链接，为讨论提供了实际案例支持。

• **色彩标准与白点问题**：[kurthr] 提出了关于白点标准的问题，指出在不同光照条件下白点的定义可能不同，这在色彩还原中是一个技术挑战。

通过这些讨论，可以看出太空图像的色彩呈现既是科学问题，也是艺术问题，涉及技术实现、主观解释和历史文化背景等多方面因素。

data.author: danielhanchen
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Qwen3-Coder，这是一款先进的代码模型，具有多个版本，其中最强大的是Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct，包含4800亿参数，支持256K tokens的上下文长度，通过外推方法可扩展至1M tokens，在编码和代理任务中表现卓越。该模型在Agentic Coding、Agentic Browser-Use和Agentic Tool-Use方面达到了最新顶尖水平，媲美Claude Sonnet 4。

此外，还开源了Qwen Code命令行工具，该工具基于Gemini Code，经过定制以充分发挥Qwen3-Coder的能力。模型在预训练和后期训练中通过扩展 tokens、上下文长度、合成数据以及强化学习等方面进行了优化，显著提升了代码执行成功率和多轮交互任务的性能。

用户可以通过npm安装Qwen Code，并使用OpenAI SDK或Claude Code与模型交互，享受高效的编码体验。

GITHUB
HUGGING FACE
MODELSCOPE
DISCORD
Today, we’re announcing Qwen3-Coder, our most agentic code model to date. Qwen3-Coder is available in multiple sizes, but we’re excited to introduce its most powerful variant first: Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct — a 480B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 35B active parameters which supports the context length of 256K tokens natively and 1M tokens with extrapolation methods, offering exceptional performance in both coding and agentic tasks. Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct sets new state-of-the-art results among open models on Agentic Coding, Agentic Browser-Use, and Agentic Tool-Use, comparable to Claude Sonnet 4.
Alongside the model, we’re also open-sourcing a command-line tool for agentic coding: Qwen Code. Forked from Gemini Code, Qwen Code has been adapted with customized prompts and function calling protocols to fully unleash the capabilities of Qwen3-Coder on agentic coding tasks. Qwen3-Coder works seamlessly with the community’s best developer tools. As a foundation model, we hope it can be used anywhere across the digital world — Agentic Coding in the World!
Qwen3-Coder
#
Pre-Training
#
There’s still room to scale in pretraining—and with Qwen3-Coder, we’re advancing along multiple dimensions to strengthen the model’s core capabilities:
Scaling Tokens: 7.5T tokens (70% code ratio), excelling in coding while preserving general and math abilities.
Scaling Context: Natively supports 256K context and can be extended up to 1M with YaRN, optimized for repo-scale and dynamic data (e.g., Pull Requests) to empower Agentic Coding.
Scaling Synthetic Data: Leveraged Qwen2.5-Coder to clean and rewrite noisy data, significantly improving overall data quality.
Post-Training
#
Scaling Code RL: Hard to Solve, Easy to Verify
#
Unlike the prevailing focus on competitive-level code generation in the community, we believe all code tasks are naturally well-suited for execution-driven large-scale reinforcement learning. That’s why we scaled up Code RL training on a broader set of real-world coding tasks. By automatically scaling test cases of diversity coding tasks, we created high-quality training instances and successfully unlocked the full potential of reinforcement learning. It not only significantly boosted code execution success rates, but also brought gains to other tasks. This encourages us to keep exploring hard-to-solve, easy-to-verify tasks as fertile ground for large-scale reinforcement learning.
Scaling Long-Horizon RL
#
In real-world software engineering tasks like SWE-Bench, Qwen3-Coder must engage in multi-turn interaction with the environment, involving planning, using tools, receiving feedback, and making decisions. In the post-training phase of Qwen3-Coder, we introduced long-horizon RL (Agent RL) to encourage the model to solve real-world tasks through multi-turn interactions using tools. The key challenge of Agent RL lies in environment scaling. To address this, we built a scalable system capable of running 20,000 independent environments in parallel, leveraging Alibaba Cloud’s infrastructure. The infrastructure provides the necessary feedback for large-scale reinforcement learning and supports evaluation at scale. As a result, Qwen3-Coder achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source models on SWE-Bench Verified without test-time scaling.
Code with Qwen3-Coder
#
Qwen Code
#
Qwen Code is a research-purpose CLI tool adapted from Gemini CLI, with enhanced parser and tool support for Qwen-Coder models.
Make sure you have installed nodejs 20+:
You could install it via the following commands:
curl -qL https://www.npmjs.com/install.sh
|
sh
Then install Qwen code via npm manager:
npm i -g @qwen-code/qwen-code
The other way is to install from the source:
git clone https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code.git
cd
qwen-code
&&
npm install
&&
npm install -g
Qwen Code supports the OpenAI SDK when calling LLMs, and you can export the following environment variables or simply put them under the
.envfile
.
export
OPENAI_API_KEY
=
"your_api_key_here"
export
OPENAI_BASE_URL
=
"https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1"
export
OPENAI_MODEL
=
"qwen3-coder-plus"
Now enjoy your vibe coding with Qwen-Code and Qwen, by simply typing: qwen!
Claude Code
#
In addition to Qwen Code, you can now use Qwen3‑Coder with Claude Code. Simply request an API key on
Alibaba Cloud Model Studio
platform and install Claude Code to start coding.
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
We have provided two entrypoints for seamlessly experiencing coding with Qwen3-Coder.
Optional 1: Claude Code proxy API
#
export
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
=
https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/api/v2/apps/claude-code-proxy
export
ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
=
your-dashscope-apikey
Then you should be able to use Claude Code with Qwen3-Coder!

data.title: Comparing the Glove80 and Maltron Keyboards
data.author: ltratt
data.article_summary: 本文比较了Glove80和Maltron两款键盘，作者因长期打字导致手部疼痛，从而关注键盘的人体工学设计。Maltron键盘通过分裂式设计和拇指键区减少手部压力，作者使用了19年后键盘外壳出现裂痕，于是尝试更换为Glove80。尽管Glove80做工精良且设计类似，但其拇指键区设计不如Maltron灵活，后者每个拇指可控制16个独立键位，显著减轻了其他手指的负担。最终，作者回归Maltron，认为其设计在 ergonomics（人体工学）上更优越。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： ergonomic键盘的设计与使用体验

不同观点：
• lukewrites认为Glove80的拇指簇和键位设计最符合他的使用习惯，能够有效缓解手部和手腕的不适。他建议通过热图分析自己的键盘使用情况，并根据个人需求调整键位布局，同时指出不必使用所有按键。
• ivanb强调了集成指向设备的重要性，认为频繁切换到鼠标会影响姿势平衡，并提出所有按键应具有独特的触感以提高准确性。他对Glove80的均匀按键设计持批评态度。
• mark_undoio对比了Maltron和Kinesis键盘，认为Maltron在人体工学设计上更为出色，尽管其外观和设计显得老旧。
• bschwarz推荐了Svalboard作为DataHand的继承者，并声称其拯救了他的职业生涯。
• zeagle对Glove80的拇指簇设计表示不满，认为其使用不便，但承认其在某些功能上的改进，如空格和退格键的设置。
• ledauphin与zeagle有相同体验，认为Glove80的拇指簇设计比Ergodox EZ更差。
• hommelix对热图分析的方法表示赞同，但提出在减少伸展的同时也应注意手指的伸展运动，以保持肌肉平衡。
• net_分享了他从标准键盘转向Glove80的经历，指出了拇指簇的问题，并建议配合轨迹球鼠标使用。
• eviks对键位布局设计和home row mods的使用提出了技术性建议，并讨论了键盘配置中的可能问题。
• lytfyre分享了他使用Kinesis Advantage系列键盘的长期经验，认为其设计有效缓解了RSI问题。
• tylermenezes高度评价Kinesis Advantage 360，认为其舒适且可定制，没有拇指键问题。
• tiltowait对Keyboardio的拇指簇和掌键设计表示赞赏，尽管其缺少Maltron和Glove80的凹面设计。
• ehnto使用Lily58键盘，认为其拇指簇设计适合手较小的人，并强调了选择合适键盘的重要性。
• kcrwfrd_喜欢Kinesis Advantage键盘，但希望有更多的拇指键以增加功能性。
• freedomdom以幽默方式提到了多种另类键盘设计，表达了对独特设计的需求。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：Glove80的拇指簇设计是否符合人体工学需求。lukewrites和zeagle等人对其表示赞赏，而ivanb和ledauphin等人则批评其设计不便。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：指向设备的重要性、键盘使用中的姿势平衡、不同键盘设计的比较、以及通过热图分析优化键位布局的方法。

Computer keyboards largely go unnoticed in daily life: most of us have to use
them at some point or another, but they tend to be seen as interchangeable
lumps of plastic and metal
1
.
For some of us, however, what keyboard we use has an effect on our health. I
have typed a
lot
, for well over 30 years. 25 years ago I had prolonged period of
pain in my hands that was, in part, brought on by extensive keyboard usage.
After 3 months of not typing at all, I resolved to do anything I could to
lessen the chance of the problem recurring. I soon realised that traditional
keyboards force our hands into an awkward diagonal posture that can cause
problems over time.
Looking around for a solution â any solution, no matter how odd it might seem! â I alighted upon
Maltron
keyboards
. I bought a PS/2 model, and then later a
USB model, and those have been my main keyboards ever since. Nearly
everyone whoâs come to my office has taken one look at the large lump of grey
plastic at the centre of my desk and asked âwhat is
that
?â:
Recently, after 19 years of very long service, my Maltron started developing
cracks in its case (which you can see in the photo above if you look
carefully). Despite the fact that it does look a bit flimsy, Iâve put more
miles into that keyboard than any other keyboard owner I know. I can hardly
complain that itâs eventually shown signs of wear, especially as I have a
tendency to rest a chunk of my body weight on it when Iâm thinking!
I took this as an opportunity to rethink my keyboard. What if, 25 years after I
last investigated this, there was a superior option? I remembered someone who I
respected waxing lyrical about the
MoErgo Glove80
keyboard
and, after some investigation of the alternatives, decided to take the plunge.
My first impressions of the Glove80 you can see above were positive. It is a
nicely manufactured piece of kit that has clearly had effort and thought put
into it. Even the keys
feel
nice! However, 3 weeks later, I have gone back to
my Maltron. Because I only found one brief comment online comparing the two
keyboards â Maltrons are a tiny niche within the broader niche of unusual
keyboards â I thought it would be worth explaining my experience, because
it seems to me that keyboard designers are missing out on superior designs.
The importance of thumbpads
What anyone who looks at a Glove80 or a Maltron will quickly notice â after theyâve
got over the initial âthatâs a weird keyboardâ reaction â is that the keyboard
is split into two. [In the Glove80âs case, this is very literal: it is two
physically separate âhalf sizeâ keyboards.] The keys are also not on the normal flat plane:
they are laid out in the inside of a gently curving bowl. The Glove80 and Maltron
have similar bowl shapes: not identical, but the differences are sufficiently
minor that I found transferring between them to have little impact on my typing
speed or accuracy.
Fewer people notice that splitting the keyboard like this makes possible a fundamental
difference over traditional keyboards: one can put multiple keys under the
thumb, what I will call a
thumbpad
2
. On a traditional keyboard, most of us will only use our thumbs for the
Space bar and, perhaps, one or two keys either side of it. Letâs be generous
and say that most of us can press 5 discrete keys between our two thumbs.
Each of my Maltronâs two thumb pads is a 3x3 grid of keys, one of which is double sized (i.e. 8
physical keys): my two thumbs can thus access 16 discrete keys:
The Glove80 puts a 3x2 grid (i.e. 6 physical keys) under each of my thumbs:
Putting more keys under our thumbs has two advantages. First, it lessens the
load on any given typing finger. Second, our thumbs are incredibly flexible
and can comfortably stretch over a much wider range than any of our other fingers.
Once you have got used to thumbpads, the difference is stark. I suspect that
thumbpads are at least as important to improved ergonomics as is the more
obvious âsplitâ between keyboard halves.
Differences in the two thumbpads
It is in the thumb pads that the Glove80 and Maltron fundamentally diverge, and they
do so in two ways. I noticed both soon after taking receipt of the Glove80, but
I didnât appreciate how much they effect me.

data.author: pepys
data.article_summary: 《亚历山大·科耶夫的生平与思想》一书介绍了20世纪重要哲学家亚历山大·科耶夫的传奇经历。科耶夫出生于1902年莫斯科一个上层资产阶级家庭，与画家瓦西里·康定斯基是亲戚。在俄国革命后，他前往国外学习，最终在巴黎定居。他继承的财产因华尔街崩盘而损失殆尽，迫使他谋生，开始销售相机。1933年，他代替友人亚历山大·科伊雷在高等实践研究院讲授黑格尔的《精神现象学》，其讲座吸引了雅克·拉康、乔治·巴塔耶、莫里斯·梅洛-庞蒂等著名学者。科耶夫的思想深刻影响了20世纪的哲学、政治学和精神分析学，尽管他本人相对鲜为人知。他的作品探讨了决定论、无神论以及人类对死亡的意识。
