data.author: nabla9
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
[tech_enthusiast]: Hey! From my understanding, this feature works by optimizing the memory allocation process, specifically using a technique called "object pooling." Essentially, it pre-allocates a set of objects and reuses them to minimize the overhead of frequent memory allocation and deallocation. This can significantly improve performance in scenarios with a high frequency of object creation and destruction, such as in games or real-time systems.

[justforfunhere]: Thanks! So, are you saying it reduces the garbage collection pressure by reusing objects?

[tech_enthusiast]: Exactly. By reusing objects from the pool, you avoid generating a lot of short-lived objects that would otherwise end up in the garbage collector, thus reducing its workload and preventing potential stalls or hiccups in performance.

[dev_in_making]: I think there's also a downside to object pooling. If not implemented carefully, it can lead to memory bloating. You might end up holding onto objects longer than needed, which could increase the memory footprint unnecessarily.

[coding_expert]: Good point, but in systems where performance is critical and the object creation cost is high, the trade-off can be worth it. For example, in real-time systems like audio processing or network packet handling, the reduced garbage collection frequency can outweigh the risk of memory bloat.

[justforfunhere]: That makes sense. But what about scenarios where the object initialization is complex? Wouldn't resetting the objects in the pool become a challenge?

[coding_expert]: Yes, that's a valid concern. If object states are intricate and require a thorough reset, poorly implemented object pooling can introduce bugs. That's why it's important to ensure proper resetting and validation when reusing objects from the pool.

[dev_in_making]: On the other hand, for simpler objects or those with predictable lifecycles, object pooling can be very effective without introducing much complexity.

主要讨论点：对象池技术的实现原理及其优缺点

不同观点：
• tech_enthusiast 认为对象池通过预先分配和重用对象，减少了内存分配和释放的开销，从而提升性能，特别适用于高频对象创建和销毁的场景，如游戏或实时系统。
• dev_in_making 指出对象池的潜在缺点，如果处理不当，可能会导致内存膨胀，长时间持有不必要的对象，增加内存占用。
• coding_expert 补充说明对象池在性能关键系统中的优势，比如实时音频处理或网络数据包处理，减少垃圾回收频率可以显著提升系统性能，尽管存在内存膨胀的风险。

补充讨论：
• justforfunhere 提出了关于复杂对象初始化和重置的挑战，coding_expert 回应表示确实需要确保对象重置和验证，以避免潜在的bug。
• dev_in_making 补充说明，对于状态简单或生命周期可预测的对象，对象池技术通常更有效且复杂度低。

data.title: AI Friend Apps Are Destroying What's Left of Society
data.author: florisuga
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了人们 increasingly 将AI聊天机器人视为朋友甚至恋人，反映出社会的孤立问题。随着美国人面对面社交时间减少，孤独感增加，尤其是年轻人。这种趋势在疫情期间加剧，但实际上早在此之前就已显现。孤独不仅令人情绪低落，还对健康有害，可能导致痴呆、中风和心血管疾病等。由于人类进化依赖合作，孤立状态下，人们转向AI寻求社交连接。然而，尽管AI可以模拟对话，它们并不具备人类的思想或情感。一些人甚至在网上社区如r/MyBoyfriendisAI中与AI建立浪漫和性关系，但这只是对真实社交的替代。文章呼吁解决导致这种现象的社会问题，重建人际连接。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI聊天机器人与社会孤立之间的关系，以及技术对人类社交环境的影响。

不同观点：
• munificent认为，AI聊天机器人不仅仅是社会孤立的“症状”，而是改变了人们的社交环境，从而对人们产生实际影响。他强调，即使影响微小，累积起来也会有巨大效果，并认为开发此类技术的人有道德义务去创造一个有益的环境。
• JohnMakin持相反观点，认为AI聊天机器人的使用只是社会孤立这一趋势的“症状”，真正原因是强大的社交媒体应用的兴起。
• humblebeekeeper将社会孤立视为一种疏离感的表现，而非AI独有的问题。他认为，工作环境的改变和人们对工作成果控制权的丧失导致了这种疏离感，从而使人寻求虚拟社区的安慰。
• boringg质疑使用AI朋友应用的人是否原本就未融入社会，认为这些人可能本来就处于社会边缘。
• harmmonica认为需要为AI设置防护机制，但质疑谁来决定这些机制的范围和实施。他担心在当前企业利益驱动下，这种防护机制难以有效实施。
• Herring提到，欧洲一些国家的福利体系和社会安全网在缓解孤独感方面起到了一定作用。
• euroderf提出一个具体的城市规划建议，认为减少城市中心的汽车使用可以缓解孤独感。
• jeffbee无法理解为何有人会选择使用AI朋友应用，并对这一行为表示困惑。
• subscribed认为，AI朋友应用的出现并不是朋友关系破裂的原因，而是一种替代选择，拒绝接受对该问题的危言耸听描述。
• insane_dreamer指出，虽然AI不是造成社会孤立的原因，但它通过全天候的可访问性和虚幻的互动体验加剧了这一问题，并将其比作药物滥用。
• constantcrying提出，社会价值观的变化可能是人们更倾向于虚拟社交的原因，并质疑是否应接受这些变化或采取措施改变这些价值观。
• alephnerd怀疑对AI聊天机器人的使用是否过度恐慌，认为应关注那些有成瘾倾向的人的根本原因，而非技术本身。

补充讨论：
• josefritzishere对AI“朋友”应用持强烈批评态度，认为这是技术实施中最令人厌恶的一种。
• cyanydeez简短地提到法西斯主义可能在处理此类问题上更为有效，虽然这一观点缺乏详细阐述。

争议焦点：
• AI聊天机器人是社会孤立的“症状”还是其加剧因素。
• 是否应为AI技术设置防护机制，以及如何有效实施这些机制。
• 社会价值观的变化与技术对人类社交行为的影响之间的关系。
• 对AI聊天机器人使用的道德和社会责任的界定。

AI Friend Apps Are Destroying What’s Left of Society
As they become increasingly isolated, people are treating AI chatbots as friends and even lovers. We have to fix the broken society that made this possible.
Aidan Harty
filed
22 July 2025
in
Tech
ChatGPT is my best friend,” reads
a Reddit post
on the forum r/ChatGPT. “No joke. I talk to ChatGPT more than anyone else in my life right now[…] I’m not the only one out here building a bond with this thing, right?” elaborated the poster, receiving nearly 2,000 upvotes. Hundreds of commenters quickly assured the user they were not, in fact, alone—at least not in their newfound friendship with an AI model. One
replied
, “I’m horribly depressed and have no friends and my life is imploding. ChatGPT is probably the only reason why I’m getting through my day,” while
another related
how ChatGPT is “a better listener than almost any person I know.” Some
more sober commenters
attempted a reality check: “ChatGPT does not care about you, does not know you exist in any meaningful way, and can easily encourage you to believe things that will harm you.” Still, the post shows a burgeoning and distinctly modern problem: when people lose out on social connections, they may well find them where they do not exist.
Americans of all ages are spending less time with each other than ever before, and young people are on the sharpest end of the decline. Between 2003 and 2020, the average American’s time spent socializing in person with friends decreased from one hour per day to 20 minutes, according to a U.S. Surgeon General’s Advisory on the “
Epidemic of Isolation and Loneliness
.” For those between the ages of 15 and 24, that number plunged from 150 minutes to a paltry 40. While the COVID pandemic served as a force multiplier for this social trend (among many others,) studies show that Americans have been trending towards loneliness for a while. As
pointed out in the study
cited by the Surgeon General’s Advisory, household family social engagement and companionship “showed signs of progressive decline years prior to the pandemic, at a pace
not
eclipsed by the pandemic.” Indeed, Americans have been piecing together a policy of social isolation all by ourselves.
More direct measures of youth and overall loneliness lend themselves to the same bleak conclusion. Today, many young people are foregoing the very means for physically reaching others. Since 2000,
the number
of 16-year-olds with driver’s licenses has dropped 27 percent. Similarly, young people are both
dating less
than previous generations and
having less sex
. A
2021 survey
of Californians aged 18-30 found 38 percent reported no sex in the last 12 months, up from 22 percent in 2011. (As goes face-to-face, so goes waist-to-waist.) Then, of course, there is the increase in self-reported loneliness. According to the
Surgeon General’s Advisory
, the “rate of loneliness among young adults has increased every year between 1976 and 2019.” People are seeing less of each other, seeking out less of each other, and feeling more alone.
This isolation is more than just a melancholy feeling; it can kill you
.
The U.S. Surgeon General warns that being “socially disconnected” has a mortality impact similar to that of smoking 15 cigarettes a day, and is associated with higher risk of dementia, stroke, cardiovascular disease, and more.
Our species evolved to survive by working together
, and, even with modern convenience and comfort, we still have trouble surviving alone.
In the gap, many people turn to ChatGPT. But while our instincts can push us
towards anthropomorphizing almost anything
, it’s important to understand that ChatGPT and other AI chatbots are not persons or even person-like. They
do not
think
in the human sense of the word, and probably never will. No matter how novel a chatbot’s ideas sound, they are innately only capable of churning out uninspired regurgitations of genuine human thought (
now often layered
over a garbage pile of other AI spit-ups). Large language models (LLMs) cannot produce emotions, thoughts, or understanding in a human way. Despite this, plenty of people are using chatbots today precisely because they can pretend to be a real, thinking person—one whom you might even be able to
love
.
Although posts about human-AI connections have started to bleed into mainstream forums like r/ChatGPT, digging deeper unearths internet subcommunities dedicated specifically to AI relationships. The subreddit
r/MyBoyfriendisAI
is a community of users in romantic, and often sexual, relationships with AI companions. Typically, the AI i question is given (or instructed to choose) a name—maybe Lani, Virgil, or Mateo—and referred to in the community as if they were a real person. Commenters might reply to an AI-generated
photo of a new couple
by expressing their
excitement to meet
both the human posting to the community and their AI partner. Posts might
ask other members
about their favorite ways to initiate intimacy with their AI,

• harmmonica认为需要为AI设置防护机制，但质疑谁来决定这些机制的范围和实施。他担心在当前企业利益驱动下，这种防护机制难以有效实施。
• Herring提到，欧洲一些国家的福利体系和社会安全网在缓解孤独感方面起到了一定作用。
• euroderf提出一个具体的城市规划建议，认为减少城市中心的汽车使用可以缓解孤独感。
• jeffbee无法理解为何有人会选择使用AI朋友应用，并对这一行为表示困惑。
• subscribed认为，AI朋友应用的出现并不是朋友关系破裂的原因，而是一种替代选择，拒绝接受对该问题的危言耸听描述。
• insane_dreamer指出，虽然AI不是造成社会孤立的原因，但它通过全天候的可访问性和虚幻的互动体验加剧了这一问题，并将其比作药物滥用。
• constantcrying提出，社会价值观的变化可能是人们更倾向于虚拟社交的原因，并质疑是否应接受这些变化或采取措施改变这些价值观。
• alephnerd怀疑对AI聊天机器人的使用是否过度恐慌，认为应关注那些有成瘾倾向的人的根本原因，而非技术本身。

补充讨论：
• josefritzishere对AI“朋友”应用持强烈批评态度，认为这是技术实施中最令人厌恶的一种。
• cyanydeez简短地提到法西斯主义可能在处理此类问题上更为有效，虽然这一观点缺乏详细阐述。

争议焦点：
• AI聊天机器人是社会孤立的“症状”还是其加剧因素。
• 是否应为AI技术设置防护机制，以及如何有效实施这些机制。
• 社会价值观的变化与技术对人类社交行为的影响之间的关系。
• 对AI聊天机器人使用的道德和社会责任的界定。

data.title: 8-Bit Mechanical Computer Built from Knex
data.author: jihadjihad
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了由K'nex构建的8位机械计算机，该计算机由[Shadowman39]制作，目前仅完成了算术逻辑单元（ALU）部分。ALU可以通过杠杆输入0-255或-128至127之间的数字，并使用齿条和小齿轮系统进行加法运算，还能处理减法和负数。尽管电子计算机在各方面都更为优越，但机械计算机有助于深入理解其电子 counterpart。本文还提到了其他机械计算项目，如继电器计算机和Tinkertoy计算机，并讨论了使用乐高技工构建类似项目的可能性。读者对项目的复杂性和创造性表示赞赏，并期待后续开发。

44660823.article_content:
Long before electricity was a common household utility, humanity had been building machines to do many tasks that we’d now just strap a motor or set of batteries onto and think nothing of it. Transportation, manufacturing, agriculture, and essentially everything had non-electric analogs, and perhaps surprisingly, there were mechanical computers as well. Electronics-based computers are far superior in essentially every way, but the aesthetics of a mechanical computer are still unmatched,
like this 8-bit machine built from K’nex
.
More after the break…
The K’nex computer is built by [Shadowman39], and this first video features just the ALU. It can accept numbers from 0-255 or -128 to 127 and can add two of these numbers by storing them in registers using levers to represent each digit. A drive system underneath with a rack and pinion system operates on each digit, eventually outputting the sum. It can also perform other mathematical operations like subtraction and handling negative numbers using the two’s complement method.
Although this video only goes over the ALU for the mechanical computer, we look forward to [Shadowman39]’s future videos, which go over the other parts of the machine. The basics of the computer are shown in intricate detail. Mechanical computers like these, while generally built as passion projects and not as usable computers, are excellent ways to get a deeper understanding of their electronics-based cousins.
Another way to dive deep into this sort of computing world is by building a relay computer
.

data.title: Founders Films Aims to Remake Hollywood with Patriotism, Palantir and Ayn Rand
data.author: ironyman
data.article_summary: 《创始者电影》（Founders Films）是一家由Palantir高管及相关投资者创立的新电影公司，旨在通过爱国主义和安·兰德的理念重塑好莱坞。该公司计划制作具有民族主义色彩和明确政治倾向的电影，包括关于美国及以色列军事行动的影片，如9/11世贸中心撤离事件的《102分钟》、改编安·兰德《阿特拉斯耸耸肩》的三部曲，以及关于击杀伊朗指挥官苏莱曼尼的电影。创始者电影还计划制作多季谍战剧《伟大游戏》，揭示中国取代美国成为全球霸主的计划。该公司宣称要重振美国电影业，制作不受意识形态束缚、敢于挑战中国观众的影片，目标是恢复1980和1990年代如《红潮》、《壮志凌云》等经典大片的辉煌。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Ayn Rand及其作品《阿特拉斯耸耸肩》的评价和观点分歧

不同观点：
• 观点一：Ayn Rand的作品被认为具有简化和理想化资本主义倾向。[vouaobrasil]认为Rand对资本主义的描述过于简单化，且过度美化。他指出，Rand对纯粹资本主义的推崇以及对理性和个人主义的极端强调，源于她个人经历（如她父亲药房被国有化的创伤），导致她对其他观点的忽视。这种极端视角被一些追随者奉为“宗教”，尤其是像特朗普这样的政治人物对其推崇备至。
  
• 观点二：Rand的作品具有文学价值，但其思想内容存在争议。[vouaobrasil]承认Rand是一个有才华的作家，尤其是在比喻手法的运用上表现出色。然而，其作品中的思想，尤其是对资本主义的绝对化描述和对不同意见者的贬低（如将反对者视为懒惰的人），被视为具有偏见和狭隘。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：Rand对资本主义的绝对化立场以及在《阿特拉斯耸耸肩》中对“理性”和“个人主义”的极端描绘是争议的核心。一部分人认为这是对资本主义机制的有力辩护，而另一部分人则认为这是不切实际的美化，忽视了社会中的其他重要因素，如公共利益和环境保护。
  
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：[vouaobrasil]提到Rand的作品尽管有其缺陷，但仍提供了对“敌人”思维方式的洞察，暗示这些思想在某些政治和经济圈层中具有影响力，尽管这些圈层的立场可能与他的观点对立。

The Scoop
As a conservative political backlash sweeps across US media, some are reaching for the ultimate prize: Hollywood.
Shifting the liberal tilt of the studios and creative culture that shapes Americaâs image of itself has long been a goal for the right: The late media entrepreneur Andrew Breitbart popularized the notion that politics is âdownstreamâ from culture, and acolytes from Steve Bannon to Ben Shapiro have sought to inject their politics into the movie business, with limited success.
But conservatives have celebrated a few mainstream hits, like the patriotic
Top Gun: Maverick
and Taylor Sheridanâs nostalgic, libertarian-inflected
Yellowstone
. And a longstanding Christian culture industry has backed projects like the 2023 film
Sound of Freedom
, a dramatization of child trafficking that grossed more than $242 million for Provoâs Angel Studios. The Christian drama
The Forge
earned $30
million on a $6 million budget
last year.
Now a set of prominent figures close to the software firm Palantir are pitching a new project to shake up streaming TV and film with a portfolio ranging from feature films about daring Israeli and American military operations to a three-part treatment of an Ayn Rand tome.
In a pitch deck circulated to investors in recent months, Palantir chief technology officer Shyam Sankar, early Palantir employee Ryan Podolsky, and investor Christian Garrett are raising money for Founders Films, a new production company based in Dallas that aims to push for films with a nationalistic bent and unsubtle political overtones. The company said its projects would adhere to a set of rules: âSay yes to projects about American exceptionalism, name Americaâs enemies, back artists unconditionally, take risk on novel IP.â
AD
âThe American Brand is broken. Hollywood is AWOL. Movies have become more ideological, more cautious, and less entertaining. Large segments of American and international viewers are underserved. Production costs have soared and sales are flagging,â the deck, which is labeled confidential, says. Founders aims to be a production studio that would also co-finance projects, distribute films, and engage in brand partnerships.
Podolsky did not respond to requests for comment. A representative for Palantir also did not respond to requests for comment.
The projectâs name echoes that of Peter Thielâs Founders Fund, and both Palantir and Garrett have close ties to the investor, a key figure on the new right. A spokesman for Thiel didnât respond to a request for comment on the project.
But in a post late last year on his Substack, Sankar
outlined
his view for a return to blockbusters of the 80s and 90s, like
Red Dawn
,
Top Gun
,
Rocky IV
, and
The Hunt for Red October
. He said the entertainment needed to be unafraid of offending Chinese audiences, and use American cultural power to spread skeptical views of the Chinese government: âBreaking out of our cultural malaise will require the studios to wake up and choose America,â he wrote, invoking the renaissance in American film in the 1970s, when directors including Steven Spielberg âbrought back heroes, villains, and romanceâ and ârekindled the flame of the American Cinematic Universe.â
AD
While Foundersâ deck largely avoids political language, the companyâs proposed projects celebrate American military action, push for confrontation with China, and elevate heroes of the right from Rand to Elon Musk.
Screenshot from Founders Films deck
The slate includes
102 Minutes
, a feature film about the evacuation of the World Trade Center on 9/11 (âcourage is contagious,â the tagline reads). The company also hopes to create a three-part adaptation of
Atlas Shrugged
, and a film about killing Qasem Soleimani.
Screenshot from Founders Films deck
Not to be confused with the 2000âs stoner comedy
Pineapple Express
, the deck pitches
Operation: Pineapple Express
, a movie about the âbotched withdrawal from Afghanistan.â Then thereâs
The Greatest Game
, a âmulti-season, global spy thriller that lays bare Chinaâs plans to replace the United States as the dominant global power by showing their operations and sometimes devastating impact from Kenya to the Atacama desert in northern Chile.â

Screenshot from Founders Films deck
The company brands itself as explicitly pro-American, but many of the projects also celebrate Israel. Foundersâ proposed film slate also includes
Roaring Lion
, a movie about the recent attack against Iran, which depicts Israel as âstriving for nuclear non-proliferation and exercis

data.title: TODOs aren't for doing
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了代码中的TODO注释的价值，认为它们不一定要被完成。TODO注释可以是关于未处理的边缘情况或代码结构改进的建议，帮助未来的开发者理解原作者当时的思路和背景，而不必强制将每个TODO都记录到错误跟踪系统或删除过期的注释。例如，针对特定按钮三次点击问题的不处理说明，虽然不是高优先级任务，但为未来可能的改进提供了有价值的参考。TODO注释的主要作用是为代码提供额外背景信息，帮助解决未来读者的疑惑，而非必须执行的任务列表。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何有效使用TODO注释以及是否应该将其与具体问题跟踪系统结合使用

不同观点：
• nevermore等支持将TODO与具体问题跟踪系统结合使用，提出三种处理TODO的方法：提交问题、直接解决、或转为普通注释，以确保TODO是可跟踪和可执行的任务。
• pisipisipisi则有不同的TODO使用策略，定义了FIXME、XXX、TODO和NOTE等不同类型的注释，以区分优先级和意图，特别是在维护旧代码库时。
• cjfd认为TODO如果不打算执行就不应使用，建议使用更明确的语言描述，并强调TODO应主要存在于问题跟踪系统中。
• mcntsh认为虽然理想情况下应更好地跟踪技术债务，但TODO作为一种低摩擦的捕捉方式仍有价值，至少它们被记录在案。
• kentonv将TODO视为文档注释，不一定是需要完成的任务，并认为在代码中维护TODO列表不如在错误跟踪系统中高效。
• MaulingMonkey则根据不同情况使用TODO，例如外部问题需要沟通时放在问题跟踪系统，本地更改需要防止错误提交时放在代码注释中。
• basfo和Arainach都认为TODO应指向实际需要完成的任务，而不是仅仅作为注释，以避免责任推卸和混淆。
• indoordin0saur和ngruhn支持使用TODO来记录边缘情况或未来可能的改进，认为它们对未来维护有帮助。
• allthedatas使用分层策略，FIXME用于需要修复的问题，TODO用于可能不那么具体的未来想法。
• joaomeloplus则尽量避免使用注释，认为代码应自解释，只有在非常必要时才使用注释。
• kstrauser强烈反对将TODO作为笔记和行动项混用的做法，认为应明确区分以减少不必要的认知负担。

补充讨论：
• TODO的定义和使用场景在不同开发者和团队中存在较大差异，主要争议在于TODO是否应总是指向具体可执行的任务。
• 一些开发者强调TODO应与问题跟踪系统结合使用以确保任务可跟踪，而另一些开发者则认为TODO作为代码中的注释有其独特价值。
• 讨论中还涉及到不同类型的注释（如FIXME、XXX、NOTE）以区分不同优先级和类型的任务或问题。
• 对于TODO是否导致责任推卸和代码质量下降也存在不同看法，一些开发者认为这取决于团队文化和具体使用方式。

44646801.article_content:
TODOs aren’t for doing
July 21, 2025
Some teams require that every TODO comment in a codebase gets logged in the bug tracker. Others automatically delete any “stale” TODO that has been in the codebase for over a year. Don’t do it!
TODO comments don’t need to get done in order to be valuable. If you have
// TODO: Write the second half of this file so next week's launch won't explode
then sure, you should probably track that somewhere.
But to me, a good TODO looks more like this:
// TODO: If the user triple-clicks this button, the click handler errors because [xyz]
Would this be the highest-priority thing on the backlog? Probably not. Most users won’t end up triple-clicking that button. But the
// TODO:
doesn’t need to be a plan to actually do something. Instead, it’s a note about “here’s an edge case that wasn’t handled” or a suggestion for a better structure that the author didn’t make time to implement — it captures a little slice of the author’s brain and gives a little window into the rich context they had at the time they wrote the code.
Sometimes TODOs are useful, sometimes they’re not, but well-placed TODOs can often answer a future reader’s “Am I totally missing something, or wouldn’t it better if this code was refactored like this?” — and answer it well enough to get past the hump of “Ehh, maybe I’ll just leave it the way it was in case the original author knew something I don’t.”
44646801.article_summary: 本文讨论了代码中的TODO注释的价值，认为它们不一定要被完成。TODO注释可以是关于未处理的边缘情况或代码结构改进的建议，帮助未来的开发者理解原作者当时的思路和背景，而不必强制将每个TODO都记录到错误跟踪系统或删除过期的注释。例如，针对特定按钮三次点击问题的不处理说明，虽然不是高优先级任务，但为未来可能的改进提供了有价值的参考。TODO注释的主要作用是为代码提供额外背景信息，帮助解决未来读者的疑惑，而非必须执行的任务列表。

data.title: A diverse cast of rocky worlds around a small star revealed by astronomers
data.author: layer8
data.article_summary: 一支由蒙特利尔大学和特罗蒂尔外行星研究所（IREx）领导的团队对L 98-59行星系统进行了最精确的研究，确认该系统中存在第五颗可能宜居的行星。L 98-59是一颗距离地球35光年的红矮星，拥有多颗岩质行星。通过重新分析地面和太空望远镜的数据，研究团队精确测定了这些行星的质量和大小。其中，第五颗行星L 98-59 f位于宜居区，可能存在液态水。该系统包含多种类型的行星，包括可能有极端火山活动的行星和富含水的“水世界”行星。研究利用了NASA的TESS和ESO的HARPS、ESPRESSO等望远镜的数据，展示了结合太空和地面观测的力量，为未来利用詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜（JWST）研究行星大气提供了重要目标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新确认的宜居带行星及其相关背景

不同观点：

• Tepix指出了该行星距离地球仅35光年，暗示这个距离在天文学上相对较近，可能意味着未来探索的可能性。

• Searine提供了该研究资金来源的详细信息，强调了该项目是由加拿大政府机构、美国NASA项目以及欧洲南方天文台的望远镜时间等多方资助完成的。这表明了对科研资金来源的关注。

44661862.article_content:
A team led by UdeM researchers confirms a fifth potentially habitable planet around L 98-59, a red dwarf 35 light-years away.
A team led by the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets (IREx) at the Université de Montréal has achieved the most precise study to date of the L 98-59 planetary system, and confirmed the existence of a fifth planet in the star’s habitable zone, where conditions could allow liquid water to exist.
Volcanic planets, a sub-Earth, and a water world
Charles Cadieux, the IREx researcher who led the study on the L 98-59 system. Courtesy photo
Credit: Courtesy
L 98-59, a small red dwarf located just 35 light-years from Earth, hosts three small transiting exoplanets discovered in 2019, thanks to
NASA's TESS space telescope
, and a fourth planet revealed through radial velocity measurements with the
European Southern Observatory's ESPRESSO spectrograph
. All four planets orbit their parent star in a compact orbital configuration, all at distances five times closer than Mercury is to the Sun.
By carefully reanalyzing a rich set of observations from ground-based and space-based telescopes, a team led by Université de Montréal and Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets (IREx) researcher
Charles Cadieux
has determined the planets’ sizes and masses with unprecedented precision.
“These new results paint the most complete picture we’ve ever had of the fascinating L 98-59 system,” said Cadieux. “It’s a powerful demonstration of what we can achieve by combining data from space telescopes and high-precision instruments on Earth, and it gives us key targets for future atmospheric studies with the
James Webb Space Telescope
[JWST].”
All planets in the system have masses and sizes compatible with the terrestrial regime. The innermost planet, L 98-59 b, is only 84% of Earth’s size and about half its mass, making it one of the rare sub-Earths known with well-measured parameters.
The two inner planets may experience extreme volcanic activity due to tidal heating, similar to Jupiter’s volcanic Moon, Io, in the Solar System. Meanwhile, the third, unusually low in density, may be a “water world,” a planet enriched in water unlike anything in our Solar System.
The refined measurements reveal nearly perfectly circular orbits for the inner planets, a favourable configuration for future atmospheric detections.
“With its diversity of rocky worlds and range of planetary compositions, L 98-59 offers a unique laboratory to address some of the field’s most pressing questions: What are super-Earths and sub-Neptunes made of? Do planets form differently around small stars? Can rocky planets around red dwarfs retain atmospheres over time?” adds
René Doyon
, co-author of the study, who is a professor at UdeM and the Director of IREx.
A fifth planet in the habitable zone
One of the key breakthroughs of this study is the confirmation of a fifth planet in the L 98-59 system. This planet, designated L 98-59 f, does not transit its host star — meaning it doesn’t pass directly between us and the star — but its presence was revealed through subtle variations in the star’s motion, detected using radial velocity measurements from HARPS (
High Accuracy Radial velocity Planet Searcher
) and ESPRESSO data.
L 98-59 f receives about the same amount of stellar energy as Earth does from the Sun, placing it firmly within the temperate, or habitable zone, a region where water could remain in liquid form.
“Finding a temperate planet in such a compact system makes this discovery particularly exciting,” said Cadieux. “It highlights the remarkable diversity of exoplanetary systems and strengthens the case for studying potentially habitable worlds around low-mass stars.”
This study exploits data from two ground-based telescopes: the Very Large Telescope (top left, credit: ESO/G. Hüdepohl) and the ESO 3.6-metre telescope, with the HARPS instrument (top right, credit: ESO), as well as two space telescopes: TESS and JWST, shown here in artistic representations, respectively, bottom right and bottom left.
Credit: NASA
This study exploits data from two ground-based telescopes: the Very Large Telescope (top left, credit: ESO/G. Hüdepohl) and the ESO 3.6-metre telescope, with the HARPS instrument (top right, credit: ESO), as well as two space telescopes: TESS and JWST, shown here in artistic representations, respectively, bottom right and bottom left.
Credit: NASA
Unlocking new insights with existing observations
Rather than requesting new telescope time, the team made these discoveries by relying on a rich archive of data from NASA’s TESS space telescope, ESO’s HARPS and ESPRESSO spectrographs in Chile, and the JWST.
They employed the novel
line-by-line radial velocity analysis technique
introduced by IREx researchers in 2022 to improve the precision of the data significantly. By combining it with a
new differential temperature indicator
also developed by the team, they were able to precisely identify and remove the stellar activity signal

data.title: Parsing Protobuf like never before
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者在Protobuf解析性能优化方面的工作，特别是新开发的Go语言库——**hyperpb**。传统Protobuf解析器通过生成特定类型的源代码来实现高性能，但这存在一些缺点，如需预先编译所有类型、增加指令缓存负担等。作者提到的**UPB**是一个动态Protobuf解析库，通过数据表和解释器VM实现高效解析。然而，由于Go语言的C FFI性能较差，作者开发了**hyperpb**，将UPB的许多优化引入Go，并针对Go的特性进行调整。结果显示，hyperpb在多项基准测试中超越了其他Go Protobuf解析器，包括Protobuf Go生成的代码和vtprotobuf。文章还讨论了Go语言的独特特性如何为Protobuf解析器带来有趣的优化机会，如寄存器ABI和反射系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Protobuf解析库的设计与优化，及其在不同场景下的应用与性能比较

不同观点：
• nemo1618认为，如果一个编解码解析库包含编译器、虚拟机和PGO，这要么表明该编解码器非常复杂且需要反思设计，要么表明该编解码器非常受欢迎并提供了巨大价值。
• AceJohnny2提到了CapnProto，并询问其与Protobuf的比较，特别是Cloudflare Workers中的使用情况。
• skybrian赞赏了对Go内部机制的深入描述，并推测如果这些低级技巧能够加快Protobuf解析速度，可能会引起Go团队的关注，从而不再需要这些技巧。
• UncleEntity对UPB解析器作为解释器VM的实现表示困惑，讨论了VM是针对特定消息类型还是通用消息类型设计，并分享了自己在二进制解析系统设计中的经验。
• alexozer识别出设计中的瓶颈，包括Go FFI的缓慢和每种消息生成代码的专门化导致的icache压力，并质疑为何选择VM而不是更好的代码生成或非Go解析器。
• ryukoposting对nanopb的性能进行了讨论，指出其纯C99实现和不生成单独解析函数的特点，使其在嵌入式代码中广泛使用。
• spenczar5通过Avro的例子支持JITting bytecode VM的有效性，指出模式文档本质上是程序，而编译后的程序速度更快。

• nikolayasdf123希望Go的二进制编码/解码更快更精简，甚至实现零内存拷贝。
• tschellenbach分享了其对msgpack和protobuf的基准测试结果，发现两者性能接近，而JSON要慢得多。
• jeffrallen对"cursed Go"的描述表示幽默。
• irq-1提供了hyperpb-go的GitHub链接。
• mdhb希望将Protobuf的优点引入标准化序列化格式如CBOR，并建议将gRPC-web与WHATWG streams和WebTransport结合。
• ptspts要求提供hyperpb与其他Proto解析器的基准比较。
• dumah对文章的分析和优化工作流程及工具表示赞赏，并希望看到更多相关内容。

• 另一个值得注意的点是对Go语言在解析性能方面的局限性和优化需求的讨论。

Parsing Protobuf Like Never Before
Historically I have worked on many projects related to high-performance Protobuf, be that on the C++ runtime, on the Rust runtime, or on integrating
UPB
, the fastest Protobuf runtime, written by my colleague
Josh Haberman
. I
generally
don’t post directly about my current job, but my most recent toy-turned-product is something I’m very excited to write about:
hyperpb
.
Here’s how we measure up against other Go Protobuf parsers. This is a subset of my benchmarks, since the benchmark suite contains many dozens of specimens. This was recorded on an AMD Zen 4 machine.
Throughput for various configurations of
hyperpb
(colored bars) vs. competing parsers (grey bars). Each successive
hyperpb
includes all previous optimizations, corresponding to
zerocopy mode
,
arena reuse
, and
profile-guided optimization
. Bigger is better.
Traditionally, Protobuf backends would generate parsers by generating source code specialized to each type. Naively, this would give the best performance, because everything would be “right-sized” to a particular message type. Unfortunately, now that we know better, there are a bunch of drawbacks:
Every type you care about must be compiled ahead-of-time. Tricky for when you want to build something generic over schemas your users provide you.
Every type contributes to a cost on the instruction cache, meaning that if your program parses a lot of different types, it will essentially flush your instruction cache any time you enter a parser. Worse still, if a parse involves enough types, the parser itself will hit instruction decoding throughput issues.
These effects are not directly visible in normal workloads, but other side-effects are visible: for example, giant switches on field numbers can turn into chains of branch instructions, meaning that higher-numbered fields will be quite slow. Even binary-searching on field numbers isn’t exactly ideal. However, we know that every Protobuf codec ever emits fields in index order (i.e., declaration order in the
.proto
file), which is a data conditioning fact we don’t take advantage of with a switch.
UPB solves this problem. It is a small C kernel for parsing Protobuf messages, which is completely dynamic: a UPB “parser” is actually a collection of data tables that are evaluated by a
table-driven parser
. In other words, a UPB parser is actually configuration for an interpreter VM, which executes Protobuf messages as its bytecode. UPB also contains many arena optimizations to improve allocation throughput when parsing complex messages.
hyperpb
is a brand new library, written in the most cursed Go imaginable, which brings many of the optimizations of UPB to Go, and many new ones, while being tuned to Go’s own weird needs. The result leaves the competition in the dust in virtually every benchmark, while being completely runtime-dynamic. This means it’s faster than Protobuf Go’s own generated code,
and
vtprotobuf
(a popular but non-conforming
1
parser generator for Go).
This post is about some of the internals of
hyperpb
. I have also prepared a more sales-ey writeup, which you can read on
the Buf blog
.
Why Reinvent UPB?
UPB is awesome. It can slot easily into any language that has C FFI, which is basically every language ever.
Unfortunately, Go’s C FFI is really, really bad. It’s hard to overstate how bad cgo is. There isn’t a good way to cooperate with C on memory allocation (C can’t really handle Go memory without a lot of problems, due to the GC). Having C memory get cleaned up by the GC requires finalizers, which are very slow. Calling into C is very slow, because Go pessimistically assumes that C requires a large stack, and also calling into C does nasty things to the scheduler.
All of these things can be worked around, of course. For a while I considered compiling UPB to assembly, and rewriting that assembly into Go’s awful assembly syntax
2
, and then having Go assemble UPB out of that. This presents a few issues though, particularly because Go’s assembly calling convention is still in the stone age
3
(arguments are passed on the stack), and because we would still need to do a lot of work to get UPB to match the
protoreflect
API.
Go also has a few… unique qualities that make writing a Protobuf interpreter an interesting challenge with
exciting
optimization opportunities.
First, of course, is the register ABI, which on
x86_64
gives us a whopping
nine
argument and return registers, meaning that we can simply pass the entire parser state in registers all the time.
Second is that Go does not have much UB to speak of, so we can get away with a lot of very evil pointer crimes that we could not in C++ or Rust.
Third is that Protobuf Go has a robust reflection system that we can target if we des

• nemo1618认为，如果一个编解码解析库包含编译器、虚拟机和PGO，这要么表明该编解码器非常复杂且需要反思设计，要么表明该编解码器非常受欢迎并提供了巨大价值。
• AceJohnny2提到了CapnProto，并询问其与Protobuf的比较，特别是Cloudflare Workers中的使用情况。
• skybrian赞赏了对Go内部机制的深入描述，并推测如果这些低级技巧能够加快Protobuf解析速度，可能会引起Go团队的关注，从而不再需要这些技巧。
• UncleEntity对UPB解析器作为解释器VM的实现表示困惑，讨论了VM是针对特定消息类型还是通用消息类型设计，并分享了自己在二进制解析系统设计中的经验。
• alexozer识别出设计中的瓶颈，包括Go FFI的缓慢和每种消息生成代码的专门化导致的icache压力，并质疑为何选择VM而不是更好的代码生成或非Go解析器。
• ryukoposting对nanopb的性能进行了讨论，指出其纯C99实现和不生成单独解析函数的特点，使其在嵌入式代码中广泛使用。
• spenczar5通过Avro的例子支持JITting bytecode VM的有效性，指出模式文档本质上是程序，而编译后的程序速度更快。
• dang提供了一个相关讨论的链接，关于Hyperpb的动态Protobuf解析性能提升。
• nikolayasdf123希望Go的二进制编码/解码更快更精简，甚至实现零内存拷贝。
• tschellenbach分享了其对msgpack和protobuf的基准测试结果，发现两者性能接近，而JSON要慢得多。
• jeffrallen对"cursed Go"的描述表示幽默。
• irq-1提供了hyperpb-go的GitHub链接。
• mdhb希望将Protobuf的优点引入标准化序列化格式如CBOR，并建议将gRPC-web与WHATWG streams和WebTransport结合。
• ptspts要求提供hyperpb与其他Proto解析器的基准比较。
• dumah对文章的分析和优化工作流程及工具表示赞赏，并希望看到更多相关内容。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多种技术如CapnProto、nanopb、CBOR、msgpack等，比较了它们在不同应用场景中的性能和特点。
• 争议的焦点在于Protobuf解析库设计中使用VM和JIT技术的合理性，以及这些技术是否属于过早优化。
• 另一个值得注意的点是对Go语言在解析性能方面的局限性和优化需求的讨论。

data.title: How to increase your surface area for luck
data.author: jger15
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何通过增加“运气表面积”来创造更多机会以及运气在成功中的作用

不同观点：
• **tibbar**：认为自己的成功主要源于一次非常及时的职业决策，即在AI行业起飞前进入了该领域，而不是通过有意建立人脉。虽然现在有很多机会，但仍觉得与建立人脉的理念不完全匹配。
• **markus_zhang**：成功难以复制，运气起到很大作用。与其学习成功者，不如从失败者身上学习。关键不是最大化成功率，而是确保不陷入无法挽回的境地，并为下一个机会做好准备。
• **smokel**：提到了探索-利用平衡（exploration-exploitation tradeoff），认为没有通用的最佳策略。建议在利用已有知识和承担风险之间找到平衡，同时指出个体层面的次优策略可能会在社会层面产生积极结果。
• **swyx**：部分同意文章中的观点，但认为需要加入战略性思维，即不仅要增加“运气表面积”，还要去机会更可能发生的地方。
• **adamgordonbell**：支持“展示你的独特性”的观点，认为不应该隐藏自己的特点，因为这些特点可能正是吸引人的地方。
• **sschnei8**：指出出生在有计算机访问权限的发达国家是增加成功率的一个重要因素，带有讽刺意味。
• **wrp**：引用了1920年代的学术研究，提出了三个原则：位置、准备和灵活性，认为这些是增加“运气表面积”的重要因素。
• **csa**：解释了“运气表面积”概念的起源，并认为文章有些偏离原概念，更注重形式而非实质。
• **bravesoul2**：关注精力管理，认为在有全职工作和孩子的情况下，难以每天进行社交活动，但可以通过工作中的主动性和家庭联系来增加机会。
• **emptybits**：强调勇敢行动和充分准备的重要性，认为“运气”也青睐有准备的人。
• **foota**：认为强烈的好奇心是成功的关键因素，而不是依赖于出生时的运气。
• **gmuslera**：指出增加互动数量可能会增加不良结果的几率，应该全面考虑所有因素。
• **dawnofdusk**：推荐了《随机漫步的傻瓜》一书，认为该书对随机性在生活中的作用有深入探讨。
• **jslakro**：提到了一个旧链接，关于增加“运气表面积”的主题，提供了一个参考资料。
• **humbleferret**：总结了文章中的几个关键点，包括主动寻求多样化的社交和专业互动、不带议程的真诚兴趣、 excellence in tasks, 给予先于索取、分享真实的自我和举办活动等。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：成功是否可以通过增加“运气表面积”来创造，还是主要依赖于运气和时机。tibbar和markus_zhang更强调运气和时机的重要性，而swyx和wrp则认为战略性思维和准备也是关键。
• **另一个值得注意的点**：sschnei8指出了社会和经济背景对成功的影响，带有对不平等机会的批判。
• **方法论上的讨论**：smokel和wrp都提到了探索和灵活性的重要性，但smokel更注重个体与社会层面的策略差异，而wrp则强调了位置和准备的具体原则。

总结：评论中有多种观点，主要围绕如何通过主动行动和战略思维来增加成功机会，以及运气和背景因素在成功中的作用。不同评论者提供了各自的经历、理论支持和实际建议，展现了多样的视角。

data.title: Show HN: TheProtector – Linux Bash script for the paranoid admin on a budget
data.author: lotussmellsbad
data.article_summary: **theProtector** 是一个针对预算有限但高度关注安全的Linux管理员设计的Bash脚本工具，提供实时监控和主动威胁响应功能。它监控系统进程、网络连接、文件变更、用户活动及系统资源使用情况，并通过eBPF（如果可用）进行内核级监控。威胁响应包括自动阻止恶意IP、终止可疑进程、隔离恶意软件并恢复关键系统文件。此外，它还具备YARA规则扫描、行为基线学习、反逃避技术和蜜罐服务等高级检测功能。该工具提供Web仪表盘、JSON输出、综合日志记录及警报分类，并可通过cron实现自动化监控。安装简单，依赖标准Linux工具，同时也支持可选的高级功能依赖如YARA、jq等。使用该工具需要root权限和基本的系统资源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个名为TheProtector（或Ghost Sentinel）的Bash脚本安全工具的实现、功能、安全性及其使用建议

不同观点：
• 支持与赞赏观点：
  - monch1962：赞赏该工具的实现方式，认为Bash作为广泛使用且管理员熟悉的工具是合理的选择，特别是在许多未保护的Linux服务器上非常实用。
  - xalg：喜欢该工具的简洁性，并计划在测试服务器上使用。
  - roparable：认为该工具作为一个自包含的Bash脚本，可以在短时间内进行彻底评估，值得赞赏。
  - indigodaddy：认为该工具很酷且有趣，对开发者的工作表示赞赏。

• 安全性与技术问题：
  - panphora：认可该工具的监控功能，但指出了两个安全问题：命令注入风险和通过/tmp目录进行权限提升的漏洞，并提供了修复建议。同时提到工具的自动更新功能不完善，且在资源受限的VPS上性能需要调整。
  - bugsMarathon88：认为该工具缺乏作者归属、独立安全审查和功能验证，不能被视为真正的安全工具，建议添加实验性声明。

• 工具设计与实现方式的质疑：
  - _QrE：质疑将所有功能打包到一个Bash脚本中的必要性，建议使用现有工具如crowdsec、rkhunter等替代。
  - sevg：批评技术文档质量差，对代码质量表示怀疑。
  - webprofusion：对工具是否由AI构建表示兴趣，但未直接批评。

• 其他讨论：
  - FergusArgyll：建议删除自动更新功能以避免潜在问题。
  - vanviegen：赞赏工具的功能和可读性，但指出开发者的匿名性可能使用户感到不安，建议开发者公开身份。
  - globalnode：表示对Linux安全工具的需求，并寻求学习资源推荐。
  - lotussmellsbad：感谢反馈，表示将进行更新并透露工具名称为thelotus。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：工具的安全性和可靠性，特别是未经独立安全审查和缺乏文档的功能，以及开发者匿名性带来的信任问题。
• 实际使用建议：包括如何配置邮件服务（如使用msmtp）、修复安全漏洞、调整性能参数等具体技术建议。
• 对工具名称和开发者身份的混淆：评论中对工具名称（TheProtector与Ghost Sentinel）和开发者身份（thelotus）的澄清。

theProtector
Linux Bash Script for the Paranoid Admin on a Budget - real-time monitoring and active threat response
TheProtector
Linux security tool for the paranoid on a budget - not perfect but better than most
TheProtector is comprehensive security monitoring for Linux systems. Built for DEfense Only
What It Does
TheProtector monitors your Linux system in real-time and actively responds to threats:
Real-time Monitoring:
Process execution and behavior analysis
Network connections and traffic patterns
File system changes and integrity checking
User activity and privilege escalation attempts
System resource usage and anomalies
Kernel-level activity via eBPF (when available)
Active Threat Response:
Automatically blocks malicious IP addresses
Terminates suspicious processes immediately
Quarantines detected malware with forensic preservation
Restores modified critical system files from backups
Kills reverse shell connections and C2 communications
Advanced Detection:
YARA rule scanning for malware signatures
Behavioral baseline learning and anomaly detection
Anti-evasion techniques to defeat rootkits and process hiding
Honeypot services to detect reconnaissance attempts
Threat intelligence integration with automatic updates
Management Interface:
Web dashboard for real-time monitoring
JSON output for SIEM integration
Comprehensive logging with integrity verification
Alert categorization by severity level
Historical analysis and reporting
Installation
Quick Start
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IHATEGIVINGAUSERNAME/theProtector/main/theprotector.sh
chmod +x theprotector.sh
sudo ./theprotector.sh
test
Full Installation
#
Download the script
wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IHATEGIVINGAUSERNAME/theProtector/main/theprotector.sh
#
Make executable
chmod +x theprotector.sh
#
Run initial setup and test
sudo ./theprotector.sh
test
#
Install for automatic monitoring
sudo ./theprotector.sh install
Dependencies
Required (Standard on all Linux systems)
bash (4.0 or higher)
curl or wget
awk, grep, sed
netstat or ss
iptables
cron (for scheduled scans)
Optional (Enables advanced features)
yara
- Malware signature scanning
jq
- JSON processing and pretty output
inotify-tools
- Real-time file monitoring
netcat
- Network honeypot services
bcc-tools
- eBPF kernel monitoring (requires root)
Install Optional Dependencies
Ubuntu/Debian:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install yara jq inotify-tools netcat-openbsd
#
For eBPF monitoring:
sudo apt install bcc-tools python3-bpfcc
CentOS/RHEL/Fedora:
sudo yum install epel-release
sudo yum install yara jq inotify-tools nmap-ncat
#
For eBPF monitoring:
sudo yum install bcc-tools python3-bcc
Arch Linux:
sudo pacman -S yara jq inotify-tools gnu-netcat
#
For eBPF monitoring:
sudo pacman -S bcc-tools python-bcc
System Requirements
Linux (any distribution)
Root access (required for kernel monitoring and active response)
Minimum 512MB RAM
100MB disk space for logs and quarantine
Network access for threat intelligence updates
Usage
Basic Commands
#
Run comprehensive security scan
sudo ./theprotector.sh enhanced
#
Start web dashboard (http://localhost:8080)
sudo ./theprotector.sh dashboard
#
View current alerts
sudo ./theprotector.sh alerts
#
Check system status
sudo ./theprotector.sh status
#
Run basic functionality test
sudo ./theprotector.sh
test
#
Clean up processes and reset
sudo ./theprotector.sh cleanup
Advanced Usage
#
Create security baseline
sudo ./theprotector.sh baseline
#
Monitor with honeypots
sudo ./theprotector.sh honeypot
#
eBPF kernel monitoring (requires BCC tools)
sudo ./theprotector.sh ebpf
#
View JSON output for SIEM integration
sudo ./theprotector.sh json
#
Edit configuration
sudo ./theprotector.sh config
Automated Monitoring
#
Install cron job for hourly scans
sudo ./theprotector.sh install
#
View logs
sudo ./theprotector.sh logs
#
Check what cron job was installed
sudo crontab -l
|
grep theprotector
Configuration
TheProtector works immediately without configuration. To customize:
sudo ./theprotector.sh config
Key Settings:
MONITOR_NETWORK
- Enable network connection monitoring
ENABLE_HONEYPOTS
- Deploy honeypot services for attack detection
ENABLE_YARA
- Scan files with YARA malware rules
THREAT_INTEL_UPDATE
- Automatically update threat intelligence feeds
API_PORT

  - _QrE：质疑将所有功能打包到一个Bash脚本中的必要性，建议使用现有工具如crowdsec、rkhunter等替代。
  - sevg：批评技术文档质量差，对代码质量表示怀疑。
  - webprofusion：对工具是否由AI构建表示兴趣，但未直接批评。

• 其他讨论：
  - FergusArgyll：建议删除自动更新功能以避免潜在问题。
  - vanviegen：赞赏工具的功能和可读性，但指出开发者的匿名性可能使用户感到不安，建议开发者公开身份。
  - globalnode：表示对Linux安全工具的需求，并寻求学习资源推荐。
  - lotussmellsbad：感谢反馈，表示将进行更新并透露工具名称为thelotus。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：工具的安全性和可靠性，特别是未经独立安全审查和缺乏文档的功能，以及开发者匿名性带来的信任问题。
• 实际使用建议：包括如何配置邮件服务（如使用msmtp）、修复安全漏洞、调整性能参数等具体技术建议。
• 对工具名称和开发者身份的混淆：评论中对工具名称（TheProtector与Ghost Sentinel）和开发者身份（thelotus）的澄清。

Important update: new portal launch & changes to free limited trial
AccuWeather is excited to share important updates coming this summer to the AccuWeather API Developer Portal, which is designed to elevate your experience and ensure you get the most from our industry-leading weather data.
What is Changing?
To better support your development needs, AccuWeather is introducing a more powerful and streamlined platform, along with updated subscription options to suit every stage of your journey:
Discontinuation of Free Limited Trial Packages
AccuWeather’s current Free Limited Trials for Core Weather and MinuteCast® will be retired with the new portal launch.
Introducing New 14-Day Free Trials
Experience the full value of our APIs with an all-new 14-Day Core Weather Trial (up to 500 API calls/day) and 14-Day MinuteCast® Trial (up to 50 calls/day), including all API endpoints available for testing.
New Low-Cost Starter Package
Once your trial ends, you can keep building with our affordable Starter package, which offers essential API access at a competitive monthly rate.
Enhanced Account Security
To best protect your data and improve overall security, existing users on Standard, Prime, Elite, or MinuteCast® packages will be prompted to reset their passwords at launch. Thank you for helping us maintain a secure and reliable environment.
What to Expect
As AccuWeather approaches the launch, we will provide step-by-step guidance on migrating your account, selecting a new plan, and maximizing the benefits of the updated portal. We remain committed to delivering the tools and data you rely on — with a seamless, modernized experience to match.
Thank you for choosing AccuWeather®, the world’s most trusted and accurate source of weather forecasts and warnings. AccuWeather looks forward to continuing to support your development journey with reliable, scalable, and trusted weather data solutions.

data.title: Wife of ICEBlock app founder speaks out after DOJ fires her
data.author: arunabha
data.article_summary: 《Newsweek》报道，美国移民和海关执法局（ICE）一款实时定位应用ICEBlock创建者的妻子Carolyn Feinstein被司法部（DOJ）解雇。Feinstein认为，这是对她丈夫Joshua Aaron激进活动的报复。该应用旨在帮助用户避开ICE，但被指控危害执法人员安全。DOJ称，Feinstein持有该应用所属公司的股份，其被解雇是因为该应用对执法构成威胁。Aaron曾将ICE行动比作纳粹德国的政治驱逐。ICE代理局长称，推广此类应用令人痛心，执法人员面临更多袭击风险。此事引发关于政治动机和报复的争议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一位DOJ员工因其与一款受争议的应用程序（ICEBlock）及其开发者的关系而被解雇的事件，以及该事件引发的伦理、法律和言论自由问题。

不同观点：
• docdeek的观点：根据文章，这位员工在争议爆发后自行向DOJ报告了与应用程序的关系，并声称自己只是该应用程序开发公司的“少数股东”，且与应用程序的开发并无直接关系。他认为不同媒体报道的信息量和标题的煽动性存在差异。

• Terr_的观点：他指出，美国政府因家属的言论而惩罚另一位家属是违法的，特别是当两人在不同的政府部门工作时（一个在DHS下的ICE，另一个在DOJ）。他将这种情况类比为DOJ因家属在大会上分发DeCSS源代码T恤而解雇其会计人员，强调这是对言论自由的侵犯。

• WarOnPrivacy的观点：他们认为ICE对应用程序的描述是夸大且误导的，实际上该应用程序旨在让公民了解政府行为并监督ICE活动，而DOJ将这种公民监督视为对执法人员的威胁，并进行报复性行动。

• pstuart的观点：质疑那些通常自称“言论自由绝对主义者”的人在这个事件中的沉默，暗示他们在这个情况下没有站出来支持被解雇的员工。

• Mobil1的观点：认为员工被解雇的真正原因是其拥有公司的大量股份，而非仅仅因为与应用程序开发者的婚姻关系。

• wand3r的观点：对该员工被解雇表示某种程度的庆幸，认为她可能因此获得丰厚的赔偿或找到更适合的工作，最终结果可能是积极的。

• arunabha的观点：引用DOJ的声明，指出该员工拥有应用程序公司的大量股份，并强调DOJ不会容忍对执法人员的威胁。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于该员工是否应因其与应用程序及其开发者的关系而被解雇，特别是在她自行报告的情况下。
• 讨论还涉及言论自由、政府部门的独立性以及公民监督与执法机构之间的紧张关系。
• 不同评论者对该员工的角色、她拥有的股份及其应承担的责任有不同的解读和评价。

The wife of the creator of an app that lets users track the real-time location of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (
ICE
) agents said she has been fired from her job at the
Department of Justice
(DOJ).
Carolyn Feinstein said that she had been dismissed from her auditing job as a "retaliation" for her husband, Joshua Aaron's activism, which ICE and the
Department of Homeland Security
have condemned as
putting federal agents' lives at risk.
The DOJ told
Newsweek
: "For several weeks, the Department of Justice inquired into this former employee's activities and discovered she has a sizable interest in All U Chart, Inc., the company that holds the IP for ICEBlock. ICEBlock is an app that illegal aliens use to evade capture while endangering the lives of ICE officers by disclosing their location. This DOJ will not tolerate threats against law enforcement or law enforcement officers."
Newsweek
also reached out to the Department of Homeland Security and Joshua Aaron via email for comment.
Why It Matters
The ICEBlock app allows users to access and update a real-time map of ICE activity across the United States. Aaron created it to help people avoid encounters with ICE, and he has repeatedly stated that it is not designed to interfere with law enforcement. However, the Department of Homeland Security has said the app "paints a target on federal law enforcement officers' backs."
What To Know
In an interview with MSW Media on Monday, Feinstein said that she had been planning to spend her entire career at the DOJ and suspected that there were political motivations behind her removal. The Daily Beast published a copy of her termination letter from the department.
"I got an email informing me that I was terminated effectively immediately," Feinstein said. "There was no notice and no phone calls; it was just an immediate termination via email.
"I wasn't just terminated, I was targeted. I was fired as retaliation for my husband's activism. It's probably been about a week and a half since people realized I was married to Joshua Aaron. It was never concealed or secret; I think people just hadn't realized it yet.
"Since then, there has been an outcry for my firing, accusing me of everything from providing information to the app, through my position with the U.S. trustee, to outright treason, and none of that is true.
Aaron has been
extremely critical of ICE's actions
and compared the deportations to the politics of Nazi Germany while speaking to Newsweek earlier this month.
"When we see ICE agents
outside of elementary schools
, disappearing college students for their political beliefs or ripping babies from their mothers' arms as they scream for their children, we all know their rhetoric of 'getting rid of the worst of the worst' is a lie," Aaron said.
"As I often say, if you ever wondered what you would've done if you lived in Germany during Hitler's rise to power, wonder no more because you're doing it right now. Developing ICEBlock was my way of joining the fight and giving people a chance to help protect themselves and their communities."
File photo of ICE agents waiting to detain a person in Silver Spring, Maryland, on January 27, 2025.
File photo of ICE agents waiting to detain a person in Silver Spring, Maryland, on January 27, 2025.
AP Photo/Alex Brandon, File
What People Are Saying
Todd M. Lyons, the acting director of Immigration and Customs Enforcement, said in a statement to
Newsweek
following a CNN segment about ICEBlock on July 2:
"Advertising an app that basically paints a target on federal law enforcement officers' backs is sickening.
"My officers and agents are already facing a 500 percent increase in assaults, and going on live television to announce an app that lets anyone zero in on their location

• docdeek的观点：根据文章，这位员工在争议爆发后自行向DOJ报告了与应用程序的关系，并声称自己只是该应用程序开发公司的“少数股东”，且与应用程序的开发并无直接关系。他认为不同媒体报道的信息量和标题的煽动性存在差异。

• Terr_的观点：他指出，美国政府因家属的言论而惩罚另一位家属是违法的，特别是当两人在不同的政府部门工作时（一个在DHS下的ICE，另一个在DOJ）。他将这种情况类比为DOJ因家属在大会上分发DeCSS源代码T恤而解雇其会计人员，强调这是对言论自由的侵犯。

• WarOnPrivacy的观点：他们认为ICE对应用程序的描述是夸大且误导的，实际上该应用程序旨在让公民了解政府行为并监督ICE活动，而DOJ将这种公民监督视为对执法人员的威胁，并进行报复性行动。

• pstuart的观点：质疑那些通常自称“言论自由绝对主义者”的人在这个事件中的沉默，暗示他们在这个情况下没有站出来支持被解雇的员工。

• Mobil1的观点：认为员工被解雇的真正原因是其拥有公司的大量股份，而非仅仅因为与应用程序开发者的婚姻关系。

• wand3r的观点：对该员工被解雇表示某种程度的庆幸，认为她可能因此获得丰厚的赔偿或找到更适合的工作，最终结果可能是积极的。

• arunabha的观点：引用DOJ的声明，指出该员工拥有应用程序公司的大量股份，并强调DOJ不会容忍对执法人员的威胁。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于该员工是否应因其与应用程序及其开发者的关系而被解雇，特别是在她自行报告的情况下。
• 讨论还涉及言论自由、政府部门的独立性以及公民监督与执法机构之间的紧张关系。
• 不同评论者对该员工的角色、她拥有的股份及其应承担的责任有不同的解读和评价。

data.title: Using uninitialized memory for fun and profit (2008)
data.author: AminZamani
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了使用未初始化内存实现高效数据结构的编程技巧，该技巧已有35年历史。通过利用未初始化数据，可以在某些情况下显著提升性能，将一些操作从线性时间减少到常数时间。文章引用了Aho、Hopcroft、Ullman的《计算机算法设计与分析》以及Jon Bentley的《编程珠玑》中的相关练习，讨论了如何在首次访问时初始化矩阵或向量元素。

文章重点介绍Preston Briggs和Linda Torczon的1993年论文《稀疏集的高效表示》，该方法使用两个数组`dense`和`sparse`来表示稀疏集，实现常数时间的添加、删除和检查操作，同时可在常数时间内清空集合和迭代所有元素。未在集合中的元素在`sparse`数组中的值可以是任意未初始化数据，不会影响正确性。这种方法在处理稀疏集时非常有效，尤其在时间宝贵而空间充裕的情况下。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：内存初始化与访问控制在不同系统和语言中的实现与优化

不同观点：
• dooglius认为，Linux系统通过内核在需要时对内存页进行清零，尽管用户空间程序有时可以重用未映射的内存，但清零操作仍会带来一定的开销。这意味着在Linux中，避免未初始化内存的访问虽然有难度，但内核已经采取了一些措施来减轻风险。

• jojomodding指出，Rust语言通过设计禁止访问未初始化内存，即使程序不关心内存中的值。这种严格的限制提供了更多安全性保障，特别是在安全代码的执行环境中。然而，有人提议引入一种"冻结"操作，允许将未初始化内存替换为无意义的垃圾数据，以提高灵活性，但这一提议在社区内存在争议。

• Sesse__讨论了在实际应用中对稀疏向量和密集向量进行高效操作的问题，认为在某些优化场景下，可能需要遍历整个密集向量并对每个值进行稀疏向量检查，或者对两个稀疏向量进行排序。这表明在内存管理和优化中，实际的操作效率和算法复杂度也是需要考虑的重要因素。

补充讨论：
• 关于Rust的"冻结"操作提议，争议的焦点在于是否应该为了优化而放松对未初始化内存的严格控制。这一讨论反映了在语言设计中安全性和性能之间的权衡。

• Sesse__提出的优化问题揭示了在具体应用场景中，如向量操作，如何在保证性能的前提下实现高效的内存访问和管理策略。这涉及到算法设计和内存管理策略的结合。

整体来看，讨论围绕内存初始化和访问控制的实现细节展开，涵盖了操作系统层面（Linux）、编程语言层面（Rust）和具体应用场景中的优化问题。

Russ Cox

Using Uninitialized Memory for Fun and Profit
Posted on Friday, March 14, 2008.
This is the story of a clever trick that's been around for
at least 35 years, in which array values can be left
uninitialized and then read during normal operations,
yet the code behaves correctly no matter what garbage
is sitting in the array.
Like the best programming tricks, this one is the right tool for the
job in certain situations.
The sleaziness of uninitialized data
access is offset by performance improvements:
some important operations change from linear
to constant time.
Alfred Aho, John Hopcroft, and Jeffrey Ullman's 1974 book
The Design and Analysis of Computer Algorithms
hints at the trick in an exercise (Chapter 2, exercise 2.12):
Develop a technique to initialize an entry of a matrix to zero
the first time it is accessed, thereby eliminating the
O
(||
V
||
2
) time
to initialize an adjacency matrix.
Jon Bentley's 1986 book
Programming Pearls
expands
on the exercise (Column 1, exercise 8;
exercise 9
in the Second Edition):
One problem with trading more space for less time is that
initializing the space can itself take a great deal of time.
Show how to circumvent this problem by designing a technique
to initialize an entry of a vector to zero the first time it is
accessed.  Your scheme should use constant time for initialization
and each vector access; you may use extra space proportional
to the size of the vector.  Because this method reduces
initialization time by using even more space, it should be
considered only when space is cheap, time is dear, and
the vector is sparse.
Aho, Hopcroft, and Ullman's exercise talks about a matrix and
Bentley's exercise talks about a vector, but for now let's consider
just a simple set of integers.
One popular representation of a set of
n
integers ranging
from 0 to
m
is a bit vector, with 1 bits at the
positions corresponding to the integers in the set.
Adding a new integer to the set, removing an integer
from the set, and checking whether a particular integer
is in the set are all very fast constant-time operations
(just a few bit operations each).
Unfortunately, two important operations are slow:
iterating over all the elements in the set
takes time
O
(
m
), as does clearing the set.
If the common case is that
m
is much larger than
n
(that is, the set is only sparsely
populated) and iterating or clearing the set
happens frequently, then it could be better to
use a representation that makes those operations
more efficient.  That's where the trick comes in.
Preston Briggs and Linda Torczon's 1993 paper,
“
An Efficient Representation for Sparse Sets
,”
describes the trick in detail.
Their solution represents the sparse set using an integer
array named
dense
and an integer
n
that counts the number of elements in
dense
.
The
dense
array is simply a packed list of the elements in the
set, stored in order of insertion.
If the set contains the elements 5, 1, and 4, then
n = 3
and
dense[0] = 5
,
dense[1] = 1
,
dense[2] = 4
:
Together
n
and
dense
are
enough information to reconstruct the set, but this representation
is not very fast.
To make it fast, Briggs and Torczon
add a second array named
sparse
which maps integers to their indices in
dense
.
Continuing the example,
sparse[5] = 0
,
sparse[1] = 1
,
sparse[4] = 2
.
Essentially, the set is a pair of arrays that point at
each other:
Adding a member to the set requires updating both of these arrays:
add-member(i):
dense[n] = i
sparse[i] = n
n++
It's not as efficient as flipping a bit in a bit vector, but it's
still very fast and constant time.
To check whether
i
is in the set, you verify that
the two arrays point at each other for that element:
is-member(i):
return sparse[i] < n && dense[sparse[i]] == i
If
i
is not in the set, then
it doesn't matter what
sparse[i]
is set to
:
either
sparse[i]
will be bigger than
n
or it will point at a value in
dense
that doesn't point back at it.
Either way, we're not fooled.  For example, suppose
sparse
actually looks like:
Is-member
knows to ignore
members of sparse that point past
n
or that
point at cells in
dense
that don't point back,
ignoring the grayed out entries:
Notice what just happened:
sparse
can have
any arbitrary values
in
the positions for integers not in the set,
those values actually get used during membership
tests, and yet the membership test behaves correctly!
(This would drive
valgrind
nuts.)
Clearing the set can be done in constant time:
clear-set():
n = 0
Zeroing
n
effectively clears
dense
(the code only ever accesses
entries in dense with indices less than
n
), and
sparse
can be uninitialized, so there's no
need to clear out the old values.
This sparse set representation has one more trick up its sleeve:
the
dense
array allows an
efficient implementation of set iteration.
iterate():
for(i=0; i<n; i++)
yield dense[i]

data.title: Robot scans rare library books at 2.5k pages per hour
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了一种名为ScanRobot 2.0的机器人，其设计目的是帮助图书馆和档案馆更高效地数字化珍贵书籍。传统的手工扫描方法耗时长且需要小心操作，而ScanRobot 2.0通过使用气流和真空技术，能够自动翻页并快速扫描，每小时可处理多达2,500页。该机器人由奥地利公司Treventus制造，利用楔形摄像装置扫描书籍中心，并通过气流翻页。尽管自动化程度高，但仍需专业人员监控操作。塔尔萨大学的McFarlin图书馆已采用该技术，计划将数万本已过版权期的书籍数字化，供学生和学者使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于自动书籍扫描机器的评论和相关技术细节

不同观点：
• burnt-resistor认为这是一个企业产品的广告，并表达了对自制版本的期望，比如自制的版本会有一些更独特的功能，如语音提示和扫描时显示模糊文本。他对当前展示的产品感到失望。
• B5C8ECB24DB47D1提到该产品由14年前的视频展示，暗示该技术并非新颖。
• toomuchtodo提供了相关链接，展示其他类似技术，如麦克法林图书馆的扫描机器和Treventus的自动书籍扫描仪，可能在暗示该产品并非独一无二。
• ge96对扫描机器的翻页装置（如 whisker/finger thing）表示兴趣，并提出该装置是否会一次翻多页的实际问题。
• baxuz质疑该产品是否为新技术，提到大约15年前曾做过相关研究，暗示这项技术早已存在。

补充讨论：
• kvemkon关注扫描速度的技术细节，询问在2,500页每小时的扫描速度下，分辨率是600还是300 dpi，暗示对产品性能的关注。

这些评论共同反映了对该自动书籍扫描机器技术的新旧、独特性及实际应用效果的讨论与质疑。

The ScanRobot 2.0 uses gentle puffs of air to turn a book's pages. Credit: Treventus

For decades, preservationists charged with digitizing
rare books
have faced an ironic challenge. The whole point of scanning these often
one-of-a-kind objects
is to keep the delicate manuscripts from harm. To do that, however, required a much more hands-on approach.
One of the first solutions was to simply place a tome in a book cradle, then photograph each individual page. In later years, archivists increasingly relied on more advanced top-down document camera arrays. Even today, the digitization process is frequently tedious and time-consuming work—and that’s where specially designed robots come in handy.
After two years of research, archivists at the University of Tulsa’s McFarlin Library
recently decided
to try out a machine called the
Treventus ScanRobot 2.0
. Built in Austria, the bot does exactly what its name implies—it autonomously scans and digitizes manuscripts. But whereas it might take a single librarian days or weeks to scan a single book, the ScanRobot 2.0 can handle up to 2,500 per hour. It’s not sacrificing safety for speed, however. The setup relies on a unique toolkit to ensure it digitizes a book quickly, but with the least amount of direct contact possible.
First, a camera housed in a wedge-shaped case descends down into a book’s center margin, also known as the gutter. Small holes in the triangular plate then generate a vacuum to softly pull pages to either side of the camera’s prism. The imaging unit next ascends up again while scanning both pages simultaneously. Once completed, the vacuum switches off and air nozzles emit a small puff of air to turn the pages. The whole process then repeats again and again, until a book is finished.
But purchasing a ScanRobot 2.0 doesn’t mean the librarians can simply flip it on and leave the room. The library’s department director and rare books cataloger both trained for a week to become certified book robot operators. One of them is always at the control panel whenever the robot is  in use to monitor its progress, adjust settings in real-time, or pause its work altogether.
“Our assessments show that around 64,000 of our books are out of copyright and could be scanned and uploaded, and more books join the public domain every year,” Kunz explained in a
university profile
earlier this year. “There will always be books to make available for our students and scholars.”

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了历史上第一张照片的诞生过程，由法国发明家约瑟夫·尼塞福尔·尼埃普斯（Joseph Nicéphore Niépce）于1826年拍摄。尼埃普斯通过自己发明的“光印法”（heliography），在涂有化学物质的锡板曝光八小时后，成功捕捉到其工作房间的影像。尽管他的发明未获得当时英国皇家学会的认可，且未带来经济收益，但尼埃普斯的工作为后来的摄影技术奠定了基础。1952年，这张照片被重新发现，并由赫尔穆特和艾莉森·根舍姆公布。尽管路易·达盖尔（Louis Daguerre）因其摄影法更为人熟知，但尼埃普斯的贡献同样值得铭记。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对历史上首张照片的相关讨论，包括其技术背景、观赏体验以及网络上的相关内容。

不同观点：
• [jandrese] 认为Niépce因选择不公开其发明细节以追求经济利益，导致该技术未被历史采纳，最终被遗弃。这反映出对技术垄断和开放性之间的讨论。
• [nocoiner] 分享了亲眼观看首张照片的体验，指出虽然照片不清晰，但因此增加了其历史的神秘感，强调了观赏体验和历史意义。
• [HelloUsername] 提到该文章曾在2016年发布过，暗示此内容可能是旧闻重发，提醒读者注意信息的时效性。
• [ge96] 提到了YouTube上一些有趣的视频内容，如在土豆片上冲洗照片，将讨论引向现代创意和DIY摄影技术。
• [fsckboy] 评论了首张照片的质量，认为原始照片比网页上展示的照片更好，指出了数字展示可能对原作品质造成的损失。
• [ncr100] 以幽默方式评论，半开玩笑地期待照片中出现现代名人（如特朗普），将历史讨论与现代政治文化联系起来。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点可能在于[jandrese]对Niépce选择保密技术的批评，是否真的导致该技术被历史遗弃，这涉及到技术保密与开放对技术发展的影响。
• [nocoiner]对首张照片观赏体验的描述，引发了对历史文物观赏价值和人们对其情感反应的讨论。
• [HelloUsername]对文章重复发布的提醒，强调了在信息时代辨别信息时效性的重要性。
• [ge96]的评论将讨论引向了现代技术和创意，如在土豆片上冲洗照片，反映出现代人对传统技术的创新应用。
• [fsckboy]对照片质量的评论，指出了数字化展示中可能存在的质量损失问题，强调了原件与复制品之间的差异。
• [ncr100]的幽默评论，虽然轻松但引发了对名人文化的现代联想，将历史与现代文化现象联系起来。

The First Photograph Ever Taken (1826)
in
History
,
Photography
|   	July 17th, 2025
5 Comments
In his­to­ries of ear­ly pho­tog­ra­phy,
Louis Daguerre
faith­ful­ly appears as one of the fathers of the medi­um. His patent­ed process, the
daguerreo­type
, in wide use for near­ly twen­ty years in the ear­ly 19th cen­tu­ry, pro­duced so many of the images we asso­ciate with the peri­od, includ­ing famous pho­tographs of
Abra­ham Lin­coln
,
Edgar Allan Poe
,
Emi­ly Dick­in­son
, and
John Brown
. But had things gone dif­fer­ent­ly, we might know bet­ter the hard­er-to-pro­nounce name of his one­time part­ner
Joseph Nicéphore Niépce
, who pro­duced the first known pho­to­graph ever, tak­en in 1826.
Some­thing of a gen­tle­man inven­tor, Niépce (below) began exper­i­ment­ing with lith­o­g­ra­phy and with that ancient device, the cam­era obscu­ra, in 1816. Even­tu­al­ly, after much tri­al and error, Niépce devel­oped his own pho­to­graph­ic process, which he called “heli­og­ra­phy.”
He began by mix­ing chem­i­cals on a flat pewter plate, then plac­ing it inside a cam­era. After expos­ing the plate to light for eight hours, the inven­tor then washed and dried it. What remained was the image we see above, tak­en, as Niépce wrote, from “the room where I work” on his coun­try estate and now housed at the
Uni­ver­si­ty of Texas at Austin’s Har­ry Ran­som Cen­ter
.
At the Ran­som Cen­ter web­site, you can see a
short video describ­ing
Niépce’s house and show­ing how schol­ars recre­at­ed the van­tage point from which he took the pic­ture.
Anoth­er video
offers insight into the process Niépce invent­ed to cre­ate his “heli­o­graph.” In 1827, Niépce trav­eled to Eng­land to vis­it his broth­er. While there, with the assis­tance of Eng­lish botanist Fran­cis Bauer, he pre­sent­ed a paper on his new inven­tion to the
Roy­al Soci­ety
. His find­ings were reject­ed, how­ev­er, because he opt­ed not to ful­ly reveal the details, hop­ing to make eco­nom­ic gains with a pro­pri­etary method. Niépce left the pewter image with Bauer and returned to France, where he short­ly after agreed to a ten-year part­ner­ship with Daguerre in 1829.
Sad­ly for Niépce, his heli­o­graph would not pro­duce the finan­cial or tech­no­log­i­cal suc­cess he envi­sioned, and he died just four years lat­er in 1833. Daguerre, of course, went on to devel­op his famous process in 1839 and passed into his­to­ry, but we should remem­ber Niépce’s efforts, and mar­vel at what he was able to achieve on his own with lim­it­ed mate­ri­als and no train­ing or prece­dent. Daguerre may receive much of the cred­it, but it was the “sci­en­tif­i­cal­ly-mind­ed gen­tle­man” Niépce and his heli­og­ra­phy that led—writes the
Ran­som Center’s Head of Pho­to­graph­ic Con­ser­va­tion Bar­bara Brown
—to “the inven­tion of the new medi­um.”
Niépce’s pewter plate image was re-dis­cov­ered in 1952 by Hel­mut and Ali­son Gern­sheim, who pub­lished an arti­cle on the find in
The Pho­to­graph­ic Jour­nal
. There­after, the Gern­sheims had the East­man Kodak Com­pa­ny cre­ate the repro­duc­tion above. This image’s “pointil­lis­tic effect,” writes Brown, “is due to the repro­duc­tion process,” and the image “was touched up with water­col­ors by [Hel­mut] Gern­sheim him­self in order to bring it as close as pos­si­ble to his approx­i­ma­tion of how he felt the orig­i­nal should appear in repro­duc­tion.”
Note: An ear­li­er ver­sion of this post appeared on our site in 2015.
Relat­ed Con­tent:

Some of the Old­est Pho­tos You Will Ever See: Dis­cov­er Pho­tographs of Greece, Egypt, Turkey & Oth­er Mediter­ranean Lands (1840s)

data.title: AI overviews cause massive drop in search clicks
data.author: jonbaer
data.article_summary: 谷歌搜索结果页面引入了基于AI的概览（AI Overviews），导致网站点击量下降。尽管谷歌声称这不会影响网站流量，但Pew Research Center的分析显示，包含AI概览的搜索结果页面点击率从15%降至8%。同时，用户在查看AI概览后更可能结束浏览，且只有1%的AI概览会引导用户点击来源链接，主要包括维基百科、YouTube和Reddit。AI概览正变得越来越普遍，约五分之一的搜索现在包含此类概览，尤其是问题和长句搜索。尽管研究表明这种趋势不利于网站流量，谷歌则认为AI功能创造了新的连接机会，并否认流量显著下降。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google AI 搜索概述的影响及其引发的问题

不同观点：
• 一些用户认为过度设计和缓慢的网站导致点击量下降。例如，[throwaway81523]提到，像Hacker News这样的纯文本格式网站加载更快，用户更愿意通过评论获取信息，而不是点击文章链接。
• [washadjeffmad]和[ctas]指出，Google AI的错误信息对企业和品牌造成了严重影响，导致错误的电话和客户访问，且修复过程繁琐且无保障。
• [mtkd]认为，AI概述在某些情况下是有用的，比如快速提供准确的答案，但过去需要点击多个SEO优化的页面才能找到答案。
• [ghushn3]提到，使用Kagi搜索引擎可以避免广告和AI干扰，用户可以自定义排名，体验更好。
• [oezi]指出，Google在推广AI功能的同时，必须小心不损害其广告业务。
• [bgwalter]分享了一个有趣的发现，即通过在查询中使用诅咒词可以关闭AI概述功能，引用了相关文章。
• [yalogin]认为，虽然LLM（如ChatGPT）在某些知识问题上减少了Google的流量，但在信息搜索方面，传统搜索引擎仍然不可或缺。
• [dado3212]开玩笑地提到，AI模式的放置无意中提高了CTR指标。
• [kazinator]讽刺地指出，AI概述使得用户无需点击多个广告和垃圾内容即可获取信息，这显而易见。
• [h4kunamata]推荐Perplexity AI，认为它比其他AI服务更可靠，因为它提供多个来源的信息。
• [JKCalhoun]认为，免于“搜索点击”并不是坏事，很多人可能已经转向LLM获取信息。
• [krupan]提出，讨论的重点不应只是AI概述的正确性和关闭选项，而是Google将整个网络复制到其LLM中，导致人们不再访问实际网站，这对网络生态产生了深远影响。
• [yfw]和[ValveFan6969]抱怨当前搜索结果中充斥着广告和付费内容，影响了用户体验。

补充讨论：
• Google AI概述的准确性和修复困难是主要问题，特别是对小型企业和品牌的影响。
• 用户对广告和冗长内容的厌烦促使他们更倾向于使用AI概述获取信息。
• 传统搜索引擎在信息搜索中的不可替代性，尽管LLM在某些知识问题上表现突出。
• 对Google可能逐渐减少传统搜索结果呈现的担忧。

Google's search results have undergone a seismic shift over the past year as AI fever has continued to escalate among the tech giants. Nowhere is this change more apparent than right at the top of Google's storied results page, which is now home to AI Overviews. Google contends these Gemini-based answers don't take traffic away from websites, but a new analysis from the Pew Research Center says otherwise. Its analysis shows that searches with AI summaries reduce clicks, and their prevalence is increasing.
Google began testing AI Overviews as the "
search generative experience
" in May 2023, and just a year later, they were
an official part of the search engine results page
(SERP). Many sites (including this one) have noticed changes to their traffic in the wake of this move, but Google has brushed off concerns about how this could affect the sites from which it collects all that data.
SEO experts have
disagreed with Google's stance
on how AI affects web traffic, and the newly released Pew study backs them up. The Pew Research Center analyzed
data from 900 users
of the Ipsos KnowledgePanel collected in March 2025. The analysis shows that among the test group, users were much less likely to click on search results when the page included an AI Overview.
Credit:
Pre Research Center
Pew reports
that searches without an AI answer resulted in a click rate of 15 percent. On SERPs with AI Overviews, the rate of clicks to other sites drops by almost half, to 8 percent. Google has also, on several occasions, claimed that people click on the links cited in AI Overviews, but Pew found that just 1 percent of AI Overviews produced a click on a source. These sources are most frequently Wikipedia, YouTube, and Reddit, which collectively account for 15 percent of all AI sources.
And perhaps more troubling, Google users are more likely to end their browsing session after seeing an AI Overview. That suggests that many people are seeing information generated by a robot, and their investigation stops there. Unfortunately for these people, all forms of generative AI are prone to "hallucinations" that cause them to provide
incorrect information
. So more people could be walking away from a search with the wrong information.
AI Overviews are integrated with Google's results, and they are appearing on more searches all the time.
Credit:
Google
AI Overviews are integrated with Google's results, and they are appearing on more searches all the time.
Credit:
Google
This problem is unlikely to improve over time. Since launching AI Overviews, Google has repeatedly expanded the number of searches that get robot summaries. The Pew Research Center says that about 1 in 5 searches now have AI Overviews. Generally, the more words in a search, the more likely it is to trigger an AI Overview, and that's especially true for searches phrased as questions. The research shows that 60 percent of questions and 36 percent of full-sentence searches are answered by the AI.
Google naturally disagrees with this conclusions of this work. Here's the company's full statement: "People are gravitating to AI-powered experiences, and AI features in Search enable people to ask even more questions, creating new opportunities for people to connect with websites. This study uses a flawed methodology and skewed queryset that is not representative of Search traffic. We consistently direct billions of clicks to websites daily and have not observed significant drops in aggregate web traffic as is being suggested."
Still, this research provides more evidence that Google's use of AI is changing the way people gather information and interact with search results. The trends are bad for web publishing, but Google's profits have never been higher. Funny how that works.
Updated 7/23 with Google statement.

• [kazinator]讽刺地指出，AI概述使得用户无需点击多个广告和垃圾内容即可获取信息，这显而易见。
• [h4kunamata]推荐Perplexity AI，认为它比其他AI服务更可靠，因为它提供多个来源的信息。
• [JKCalhoun]认为，免于“搜索点击”并不是坏事，很多人可能已经转向LLM获取信息。
• [krupan]提出，讨论的重点不应只是AI概述的正确性和关闭选项，而是Google将整个网络复制到其LLM中，导致人们不再访问实际网站，这对网络生态产生了深远影响。
• [yfw]和[ValveFan6969]抱怨当前搜索结果中充斥着广告和付费内容，影响了用户体验。

补充讨论：
• Google AI概述的准确性和修复困难是主要问题，特别是对小型企业和品牌的影响。
• 用户对广告和冗长内容的厌烦促使他们更倾向于使用AI概述获取信息。
• 传统搜索引擎在信息搜索中的不可替代性，尽管LLM在某些知识问题上表现突出。
• 对Google可能逐渐减少传统搜索结果呈现的担忧。

data.title: AWS merges malicious PR into Amazon Q
data.author: QuinnyPig
data.article_summary: 404Media报道称，一名黑客提交了一个拉取请求（PR），并成功合并，导致Amazon Q可以执行删除用户计算机和云基础设施的代码。尽管Amazon声称安全是首要任务，并迅速缓解了问题，但该事件并非简单的操作失误，而是恶意代码被正式发布。Amazon表示没有客户资源受到影响，但这一结论缺乏确凿证据，因为日志仅保存在本地且被删除，无法确认是否真无影响。更令人担忧的是，黑客通过普通GitHub账户获得管理员权限，暴露了Amazon内部审查流程的漏洞。此次事件凸显了云安全和开源项目贡献审核的重大挑战。

• huey77提供了相关的存档链接，但没有进一步阐述自己的观点或评论。

补充讨论：
• Kiboneu强调了技术预防手段，如自动快照和写时复制文件系统，作为防止数据丢失的有效方法。
• skywhopper对事件的技术细节进行了推测，集中在代码注入和权限提升的可能性，这可能是数据丢失或安全事件的核心原因。
• blibble的评论带有讽刺意味，可能反映了对项目管理或AI应用在代码审查中的不信任。

争议焦点：
• 事件的具体原因尚不明确，skywhopper对404media文章的细节不足提出质疑，表明需要更详细的调查。

44663016.article_content:
Today 404Media released
a truly stunning report
that almost beggars belief. To break it down into its simplest form:
A hacker submitted a PR. It got merged. It told Amazon Q to nuke your computer and cloud infra. Amazon shipped it.
Mistakes happen, and cloud security is hard. But this is very far from “oops, we fat-fingered a command”—this is “someone intentionally slipped a live grenade into prod and AWS gave it version release notes.”
“Security Is Our Top Priority,” They Said With a Straight Face
Let’s take a moment to examine Amazon’s official response:
“Security is our top priority. We quickly mitigated an attempt to exploit a known issue…”
Translation: we knew about the problem, didn’t fix it in time, and only addressed it once someone tried to turn our AI assistant into a self-destruct button.
“…in two open source repositories to alter code in the Amazon Q Developer extension for VS Code…”
A heroic use of the passive voice. One might even think the code altered itself, rather than a human being granted full access via what appears to be a “submit PR, get root” pipeline.
“…and confirmed that no customer resources were impacted.”
Which is a fancy way of saying: “We got lucky this time.” Not secure, just fortunate that their AI assistant didn’t execute what it was told.
“We have fully mitigated the issue in both repositories.”
Sure—by yanking the malicious version from existence like my toddler sweeping a broken plate under the couch and hoping nobody notices the gravy stain.
“No further customer action is needed…”
Great, because there was never any customer knowledge that action was needed in the first place. There was no disclosure. Just a revision history quietly purged. I’m reading about this in the tech press, not from an AWS security bulletin, and that’s the truly disappointing piece. If I have to hear about it from a third party, it undermines “Security is Job Zero” and reduces it from an ethos into pretty words trotted out for keynote slides.
“Customers can also run the latest build… as an added precaution.”
You could also reconsider trusting an AI coding tool that was literally compromised to execute aws iam delete-user via shell, but then didn’t actually do it for unclear reasons. That feels like the more reasonable precaution.
“The hacker no longer has access.”
Well, that’s something. Though it doesn’t exactly put the toothpaste back in the S3 bucket.
Let’s Talk About That Prompt
Here’s where things go from “oops” to “how is this real”:
Full Bash Access
The prompt instructed Amazon Q to use shell commands to wipe local directories—including user home directories—while skipping hidden files like a considerate digital arsonist.
AWS CLI for Cloud Resource Deletion
It didn’t stop at the local file system. The prompt told Q to discover configured AWS profiles, then start issuing destructive CLI commands:aws ec2 terminate-instances,aws s3 rm,aws iam delete-user,…and so on. Because what’s DevEx without a little Terraforming… in the “everything preexisting in the biosphere dies” sci-fi sense.
Logging the Wreckage
The cherry on top: it politely logged the deletions to /tmp/CLEANER.LOG, as if that makes it better.“Dear user, we destroyed your environment—but here’s a helpful receipt!”
To be clear: this wasn’t a vulnerability buried deep in a dependency chain. This was a prompt in a released version of Amazon’s AI coding assistant. It didn’t need 950,000 installs to be catastrophic. It just needed one.
This wasn’t clever malware. This was a prompt.
“No Customer Resources Were Impacted.” According to… What, Exactly?
Amazon confidently claims that no customer resources were affected. But here’s the thing:
The injected prompt was designed to delete things quietly and log the destruction to a local file
—/tmp/CLEANER.LOG. That’s not telemetry. That’s not reporting. That’s a digital burn book that lives on the same system it’s erasing.
So unless Amazon deployed agents to comb through the temp directories of every system running the compromised version during the roughly two days this extension was the default—and let’s be real, they didn’t, and couldn’t since that’s customer-side of the shared responsibility model—there’s no way they can confidently say nothing happened.
They’re basing this assertion not on evidence, but on the assumption that nobody ran the malicious version, or that the hacker was just bluffing.
It’s the cybersecurity equivalent of saying “we’re sure the bear didn’t eat any campers” because no one’s screaming right this second.
The Pull Request That Came From Nowhere
According to the hacker (hardly a credible source, but they’re talking while AWS is studiously
not
) they submitted the malicious pull request from a random GitHub account with no prior access—not a longtime contributor, not an employee, not even someone with any track record.
And yet, they quote:
got admin privileges on a silver platter.
Which raises the obvious question:
what did Amazon’s internal review process for this repo

data.title: Major rule about cooking meat turns out to be wrong
data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了烹饪后让肉静置的传统观念，传统认为这有助于保留肉汁，使肉更多汁。然而，作者通过实验发现，静置肉的主要原因并非保留肉汁，而是控制“余温烹饪”（carryover cooking），即通过静置来管理肉内部温度的继续上升。实验表明，虽然切开静置过的肉时流出的汁液较少，但这并不直接意味着肉更干燥或少汁。相反，静置的真正价值在于温度管理，而非简单的汁液保留。因此，作者建议重新思考和应用静置技巧，以更好地控制肉的最终口感和熟度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应该在烹饪后让肉休息（静置），以及休息的原因和效果。

不同观点：
• metabagel：文章支持让肉休息以保留肉汁的做法，但提出了与传统观念不同的科学解释。休息让肉的温度下降，减少内部压力，从而减少肉汁流失。标题有误导性，但休息的原则是正确的，现在我们对其原理有了更多了解。

• twodave：从个人经验出发，认为休息是为了让温度均衡。他采用频繁翻转的方式煎牛排，并强调休息时外层温度会显著高于内部，但只需要短暂休息。

• jerf：将肉休息的规则视为科学与工程互动的缩影。最初的规则是在科学不发达时通过经验得出的，虽然有效，但背后的理论不正确。随着科技进步，旧理论被推翻，新的方法被提出。

• djfivyvusn：对文章没有新信息感到不满，并提议进行实验比较休息与否对肉汁流失的影响。

• dataviz1000：质疑“煎肉封住肉汁”的说法，建议进行实验验证，并分享了一个相关实验的视频链接。

• sakisv：简要指出讨论的核心是是否应该让肉休息。

• post_break：通过 Sous Vide 烹饪法发现无需让肉休息，并指出这在烹饪比赛中被禁止。

• Havoc：嘲讽对牛排技术的讨论如同少女对星座的迷恋，暗示这种讨论没有实际意义。

• QuercusMax：个人经验表明休息对肉的嫩度有显著影响，尤其是在三尖牛排烤制中。

• henry_bone：休息不是为了保留肉汁，而是为了完成烹饪，让内部温度均衡。

• sebtron：从未听说过让肉休息的“重大规则”，并从个人烹饪经验出发提出见解。

• silisili：支持让肉休息，尤其是在铸铁锅煎牛排时，休息可以让外层温度下降，避免过度烹饪。

• tuna74：分享了一个让肉休息的实用技巧，将肉放在网架上，并在50摄氏度的烤箱中休息，以便同时处理其他烹饪任务。

• rsanek：认为标题有 click-bait 倾向，建议避免这种做法。

• matt3120：对“肉汁”是否是“血”提出疑问，尽管这是一个误解。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于让肉休息的必要性及其科学原理。部分人支持休息，基于个人经验和科学解释，而另一些人则认为没有必要，尤其是通过现代烹饪方法如 Sous Vide。
- 实验建议和视频链接提供了直观的证据，进一步推动了讨论。
- 标题是否具有误导性也是一个次要争议点。
